comment: Plain-English headlines + summaries per motion, generated by `python -m ingest.summarize_motions` and merged into docs/data*.json by build_dataset. Keyed by a content hash of the motion (see summarize_motions.motion_key) — NOT by motion id, which renumbers. Safe to hand-edit: a corrected entry is never overwritten unless you pass --force.

001ec9fe12aed779.headline: Two items pulled off the consent agenda
001ec9fe12aed779.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling two items out for separate discussion.
001ec9fe12aed779.impact: A scheduling step that decides which items get debated aloud. It touches how the meeting ran, not your street or your bill.

00f4aee32d7d1f3c.headline: Land moved from Cedar Fort into Eagle Mountain
00f4aee32d7d1f3c.summary: The council moved a piece of property out of the Town of Cedar Fort and into Eagle Mountain's city boundaries.
00f4aee32d7d1f3c.impact: If you own or live on that land, Eagle Mountain now provides your city services and sets your taxes and zoning rules instead of Cedar Fort. The motion doesn't identify the property.

010cc8116542304e.headline: Charlotte Ducos gets a two-year board term
010cc8116542304e.summary: The council appointed Charlotte Ducos to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2028.
010cc8116542304e.impact: Staggered terms keep the board from turning over all at once. That is the whole effect of this one.

024c282a213d4f6c.headline: Senior advisory seat filled through 2027
024c282a213d4f6c.summary: The council appointed Karan Heffelfinger to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council for a four-year term ending in December 2027.
024c282a213d4f6c.impact: Seniors who use city programs gain one more voice advising the council. For everyone else, nothing shifts.

02abc16bd2b9b448.headline: Mid-Valley reinvestment area plan adopted
02abc16bd2b9b448.summary: Eagle Mountain adopted the Mid-Valley Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan as its official plan for that area, contingent on the redevelopment agency approving it first.
02abc16bd2b9b448.impact: The plan is the rulebook for what happens in the Mid-Valley project area. Public notice of it goes out as state law requires, and the redevelopment agency has to sign off before it holds.

03102490b6f271b6.headline: Debra Kimbrough joins the Senior Advisory Board
03102490b6f271b6.summary: The council appointed Debra Kimbrough to a three-year term on the Senior Advisory Board, running April 2026 through March 2029.
03102490b6f271b6.impact: One seat filled on a volunteer board. Residents feel nothing from the appointment itself.

0355882506985103.headline: School district agreement restated a third time
0355882506985103.summary: The council ran the same three-city school district agreement through a third resolution, again acknowledging the central district being formed by Alpine, Highland, Cedar Hills, Lehi and American Fork.
0355882506985103.impact: Duplicate paperwork on a decision that matters: the schools your children attend are what is at stake, but this particular item adds nothing to it.

045508bfe3480d39.headline: Casitas and garage apartments allowed
045508bfe3480d39.summary: The city approved rules allowing a second dwelling inside a house, over a detached garage, or in a standalone casita, with parking for two vehicles required.
045508bfe3480d39.impact: If you want a rental casita or a unit above your garage, this sets where it may go and requires two off-street spaces. Your lot's zoning still has to permit it.

049228c18a1c7172.headline: QTS development agreement amended
049228c18a1c7172.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's development agreement with QTS; the motion doesn't say what the amendment changes.
049228c18a1c7172.impact: A development agreement sets what a company may build and what it owes the city, so changes here can matter. The record doesn't say what was changed.

04ec27e777c8cb4b.headline: New paperwork rules for subdivision and site plans
04ec27e777c8cb4b.summary: The city rewrote what applicants must submit with preliminary plats, final plats, and site plan reviews.
04ec27e777c8cb4b.impact: Developers and anyone splitting a lot will file a different set of documents. If you are not submitting plans to the city, this passes you by.

04ffe30331fff727.headline: New rules for second kitchens in homes
04ffe30331fff727.summary: The city added a new section to its code, Chapter 17.69, setting rules for second kitchens and kitchenettes in homes.
04ffe30331fff727.impact: If you have or are planning a second kitchen in your house, it is now regulated by the city. The motion itself doesn't spell out the requirements, so check with the planning department before building one.

05791ef29bb484c7.headline: Public comment set on new school district
05791ef29bb484c7.summary: The council formally accepted a feasibility study on creating a new school district and scheduled public comment for June 13 and June 18, 2024, ahead of a final decision.
05791ef29bb484c7.impact: If you have kids in school or pay property taxes here, those two dates are your chance to weigh in before the council decides whether to create the district.

05b2b8cf12484072.headline: City backs moving the rodeo grounds
05b2b8cf12484072.summary: The council declared its intent to work with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape committee on relocating the city rodeo grounds into the buffer area around Camp Williams.
05b2b8cf12484072.impact: Nothing moves yet. This only commits the city to work with the partner group on a possible new site. If you use the rodeo grounds, expect a relocation plan to come back for a real decision later.

05b7a0e34797dda9.headline: Gas power plant approved on Pony Express Parkway
05b7a0e34797dda9.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Will-Power UT for a natural gas power plant, limited to simple-cycle technology and required to be running within five years.
05b7a0e34797dda9.impact: A gas-fired power plant is now cleared to be built, with trees required along Pony Express Parkway. If you live nearby, expect construction within the next five years unless the company gets an extension.

05e56835da36deb9.headline: Rules for shops and apartments put on hold
05e56835da36deb9.summary: The council tabled changes to the city's design standards for commercial buildings and apartments, waiting on final edits from its October 21 discussion.
05e56835da36deb9.impact: Anyone planning a store or an apartment project keeps building under the current standards until the council picks the item back up. Homeowners are untouched either way.

07480df28e49ae05.headline: City to explore a shared justice court
07480df28e49ae05.summary: The council put pursuing a justice court with Utah County on its list of legislative priorities.
07480df28e49ae05.impact: A justice court would decide traffic tickets and small local cases closer to home, but this only adds it to the wish list. Nothing is set up yet.

07aab5d2e036d00d.headline: Council to be told when concept plans reach Planning
07aab5d2e036d00d.summary: The council changed the city code so it must be notified every time a concept plan is set to go before the Planning Commission.
07aab5d2e036d00d.impact: This one lands on city staff, who now have to send council a heads-up on each concept plan. Nothing changes for you as a resident, though elected members will see early development ideas sooner.

07e05b70e32db99f.headline: Consent agenda approved
07e05b70e32db99f.summary: Everything grouped on the consent agenda passed in a single vote, with the record here not listing the individual items it held.
07e05b70e32db99f.impact: Consent items are the ones no councilmember pulled out for debate. Nothing on this list reaches you.

088cec0df8eae363.headline: Join Utah Valley housing grant group
088cec0df8eae363.summary: Eagle Mountain signed on to the Utah Valley HOME Consortium, an agreement with other Utah County governments to take part in federal housing money.
088cec0df8eae363.impact: Joining the consortium is an agreement between governments, not a program with an address or a price tag attached. Nothing on your street changes because of this vote.

08965103f564aace.headline: Gina Olsen named city recorder
08965103f564aace.summary: The council adopted its consent agenda with two changes from the work session: revisions to the fiscal year financial audit and the appointment of Gina Olsen as city recorder.
08965103f564aace.impact: Olsen now keeps the city's official records and handles public records requests, so hers is the office you deal with when you ask for a document. The audit change is bookkeeping.

08e94283a45399db.headline: Building and construction rules updated
08e94283a45399db.summary: The council changed the city's building and construction rules in Title 15 of the municipal code; the record does not spell out what changed.
08e94283a45399db.impact: If you are building or remodeling, the rules you have to follow have shifted, though the meeting record does not say how. Most residents will notice nothing.

096d839c99c68bdf.headline: Development agreement with Flagship Homes approved
096d839c99c68bdf.summary: The city approved a development agreement with homebuilder Flagship Homes; the motion itself names no location, acreage, or number of homes.
096d839c99c68bdf.impact: A development agreement locks in the terms a builder must follow before it breaks ground. The motion doesn't say where this project sits or how many homes it covers, so the effect on any one neighborhood is unclear.

0a02f1c779cb9430.headline: Triple Tail redevelopment plan adopted
0a02f1c779cb9430.summary: The city adopted the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, covering 24 parcels, to steer that land toward new development and economic uses.
0a02f1c779cb9430.impact: If you live near 4000 North and Pole Canyon Boulevard east of Tyson Parkway, or south of 1000 North east of Pony Express Parkway, expect the city to actively pursue development on the land around you.

0bb5dad0d7a7d643.headline: Outdoor watering banned in part of the city
0bb5dad0d7a7d643.summary: The city put a short-term ban on outdoor water use in one area of Eagle Mountain, still allowing water for animals, hand-watered gardens, and drip irrigation.
0bb5dad0d7a7d643.impact: If you live in the affected area, you cannot water your lawn or use water outdoors until the ban lifts. You can still water animals, hand-water a garden, and run drip irrigation. The rest of the city is unaffected.

0be13cbd1051ab08.headline: Youth council members appointed
0be13cbd1051ab08.summary: The city seated new Youth City Council members, who serve until the next Youth Council election.
0be13cbd1051ab08.impact: This one matters to the teenagers who applied and their families. City services and your wallet are untouched.

0c147e143b656d14.headline: Eagle Square shopping center plat delayed
0c147e143b656d14.summary: The council held off on approving the layout for the Eagle Square commercial development until legal wording in the developer agreement is sorted out.
0c147e143b656d14.impact: Construction at Eagle Square cannot move forward until the council takes this up again. Nearby residents see no change in the meantime.

0c5f723addeb7f5c.headline: Moderate income housing plan updated
0c5f723addeb7f5c.summary: The council amended the housing section of the general plan covering moderate income housing, the state-required chapter on homes for middle and lower earners.
0c5f723addeb7f5c.impact: Utah requires every city to keep this chapter current and file it with the state. Developers and planners work from it; you will not feel it at home.

0c7c1eea2ca1c94c.headline: Senior housing zone sent back for more talk
0c7c1eea2ca1c94c.summary: The council delayed a decision on a senior housing overlay zone and asked staff to bring it back to a work session for more discussion.
0c7c1eea2ca1c94c.impact: The rules for senior housing are still unwritten, so no property is affected today. If where such projects could go matters to you, the next conversation is at a work session.

0cd454b6f97c2306.headline: Adelle Curtis joins the Library Board
0cd454b6f97c2306.summary: The council filled a Library Board seat with Adelle Curtis, a two-year term running through December 2025.
0cd454b6f97c2306.impact: A volunteer seat gets an occupant. Library hours, cards and programs carry on unchanged.

0db6f7e97ac84b03.headline: Four items pulled off the consent agenda
0db6f7e97ac84b03.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pushed two sets of minutes to a later meeting and pulled the Firefly water tank change order and a Pole Canyon annexation out for discussion.
0db6f7e97ac84b03.impact: Two items residents may care about, a water tank cost change and the annexation of 178 acres into the Pole Canyon district, were moved out for open debate rather than passed in a batch.

0e288f8eb26a6482.headline: Street connection and site plan rules changed
0e288f8eb26a6482.summary: The council changed two sections of city code covering how streets must connect between developments and the standards a site plan has to meet.
0e288f8eb26a6482.impact: Developers and their engineers work to these rules when laying out new streets and lots. The motion does not say what the standards now require, so no effect on an existing homeowner can be stated.

0e5c9773fb602a5b.headline: Rules wanted for selling off city land
0e5c9773fb602a5b.summary: The council put a written policy for judging applications to buy city-owned land on its list of legislative priorities, so staff review such requests consistently.
0e5c9773fb602a5b.impact: Nothing changes for you today. If the policy gets written, anyone asking to buy a piece of city ground would face one standard instead of a case-by-case judgment call.

0e99c5b5d094e625.headline: City to dispose of 2.15 acres of land
0e99c5b5d094e625.summary: The council approved disposing of 2.15 acres of city-owned land at Utah County parcel 59:044:0015 and set the terms.
0e99c5b5d094e625.impact: This land leaves city hands. The motion does not say who receives it or what will go there, so there is nothing concrete yet for neighbors to plan around.

0f4b0b622fb14d15.headline: Wendy's approved at 4302 Pony Express Parkway
0f4b0b622fb14d15.summary: A site plan for a Wendy's at 4302 Pony Express Parkway was approved, with conditions covering two trees on the north side, crosswalk lighting and building lights.
0f4b0b622fb14d15.impact: Drivers and neighbors near that stretch of Pony Express Parkway get a new restaurant, with a lit crosswalk on the site. Elsewhere in the city, no difference.

0f5f22581bcf6ce2.headline: Sweetwater #4 tax increment agreement signed
0f5f22581bcf6ce2.summary: The city signed an agreement with its own Redevelopment Agency covering how property taxes generated inside the Sweetwater #4 project area are collected and handed over.
0f5f22581bcf6ce2.impact: This sets the route the money takes between two arms of city government. Your tax bill is not changed by it, and finance staff handle the rest.

0f65e7bcb0db82ab.headline: Steve Conger appointed to Community Services
0f65e7bcb0db82ab.summary: The council appointed Steve Conger to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2029.
0f65e7bcb0db82ab.impact: Another advisory seat filled for three years. Day to day, you will notice nothing.

1085e33ad2393a03.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook zoning change put on hold
1085e33ad2393a03.summary: The council set aside a zoning change for the Cedar Valley Holbrook property without voting it up or down.
1085e33ad2393a03.impact: Nothing changes on that land for now. Neighbors who came to weigh in will have to watch for the item to return to a future agenda.

10ccef440f602d9d.headline: Four items pulled off the consent list
10ccef440f602d9d.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled four items out of it for open discussion later in the meeting.
10ccef440f602d9d.impact: Those four items got debated in public rather than passing in a single silent vote. The step itself reaches no resident directly.

10f1acd70c87dc7a.headline: City can hire brokers to buy and sell land
10f1acd70c87dc7a.summary: Staff were authorized to hire an outside real estate brokerage or attorney when the city buys or sells significant property.
10f1acd70c87dc7a.impact: Big city land deals will now run through a paid outside broker or lawyer rather than staff alone. Residents see nothing directly, though it shapes how the city handles the property it owns.

1157520139222e49.headline: Bryan Free joins the Planning Commission for a year
1157520139222e49.summary: The council agreed to Bryan Free serving on the Planning Commission for a one-year term running through December 2026.
1157520139222e49.impact: The Planning Commission reviews zoning and building proposals before they reach the council, so anyone following a development near them may see this name on hearing agendas.

11c56b47b1321591.headline: Overland development agreement amended again
11c56b47b1321591.summary: The council approved a fifth amendment to the Overland master development agreement, the contract that sets the terms for building that project.
11c56b47b1321591.impact: What the amendment changes is not stated in the motion, so this vote alone will not tell you what shifts on the ground. It binds the city and the developer behind Overland.

11c6491142ddab9b.headline: Same school district deal, second resolution
11c6491142ddab9b.summary: The council handled the same April 29 agreement with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield Town under a second resolution number, with the same nod to the five-city district to the north.
11c6491142ddab9b.impact: The substance is the school district agreement recorded again under another number. Nothing here reaches you beyond what that agreement already does.

12bc3ca6fe380d6f.headline: Consent agenda passed, one fee raised to $2,000
12bc3ca6fe380d6f.summary: The council approved its bundle of routine items after pulling three out for separate debate, and raised one fee from $250 to $2,000.
12bc3ca6fe380d6f.impact: Whoever pays that fee will now owe $2,000 instead of $250, and one purchase agreement had to be signed by May 27. The motion doesn't say what the fee covers, so most residents will see no change.

132335f0906ee7ed.headline: Consent agenda approved
132335f0906ee7ed.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together without separate discussion.
132335f0906ee7ed.impact: The motion text does not list what was in the batch, so there is nothing here to tell you about. Items grouped this way are usually the meeting's housekeeping.

13b4b87f46d5ada3.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 zoning change put off
13b4b87f46d5ada3.summary: The council delayed a zoning change for the land known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 and left the public hearing open.
13b4b87f46d5ada3.impact: If you live near Cedar Corners, you still have a chance to speak: the hearing was continued rather than closed. The zoning on that ground is unchanged for now.

141ef92eb43cc5b4.headline: Towns at Brylee Farms deal put on hold
141ef92eb43cc5b4.summary: The council delayed a decision on the development agreement for Towns at Brylee Farms, setting it aside without voting it up or down.
141ef92eb43cc5b4.impact: Neighbors of the site and the builder both wait. The agreement can come back to a future meeting, so nothing about the project is settled either way.

141fb27cfde742d2.headline: Fence and screening rules changed
141fb27cfde742d2.summary: The city changed the part of its code that governs fences and screening, though the motion does not spell out the new provisions.
141fb27cfde742d2.impact: If you are putting up a fence or screening on your property anywhere in the city, check the current code before you build. The rules that apply to you have changed.

1437e36981270e98.headline: Consent agenda approved
1437e36981270e98.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the bundle of items passed together in one vote; the record does not list what was in it.
1437e36981270e98.impact: Nothing in the record points to a specific change for residents, because the items grouped into this single vote were not listed.

14bfd952effb0b0c.headline: Consent agenda approved
14bfd952effb0b0c.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling one item out for separate discussion and changing another item's effective date to the date of closing.
14bfd952effb0b0c.impact: This is routine housekeeping: the batch of items the council passes without separate debate. Nothing here changes for residents on its own.

14dea4e84b22e24e.headline: New parking and screening rules citywide
14dea4e84b22e24e.summary: The city rewrote its parking and landscaping rules, requiring screening plants at least 3.5 feet tall when planted and vegetation that screens year-round.
14dea4e84b22e24e.impact: This mostly affects builders and businesses planning new lots. Where a project sits next to homes, screening plants must already be 3.5 feet tall and stay green through the winter.

1546234f3d654fa7.headline: Susan Allen named senior citizen advisor
1546234f3d654fa7.summary: Susan Allen was appointed as a Senior Citizen Advisor, with the term running through December 31, 2025.
1546234f3d654fa7.impact: One advisory seat, filled for the rest of the year. Your taxes, your property and your city services are untouched by it.

162d6b9af76b57b2.headline: "Newspaper" update to subdivision and zoning code
162d6b9af76b57b2.summary: The council amended two chapters of city code, 16.05 on subdivisions and 17.05 on zoning, in what the city calls the Newspaper Amendment.
162d6b9af76b57b2.impact: The motion does not say what the amendment actually changes, so there is nothing concrete residents will see or do differently based on this text alone.

17abba79553f22e5.headline: $190K more for the Firefly water tank
17abba79553f22e5.summary: The council took up a change order adding $189,985.67 to the cost of the Firefly 4-million-gallon water tank.
17abba79553f22e5.impact: This adds money to a city water storage tank already under contract. The motion sets no change to your water bill, and the record does not show a final outcome.

17e40cd736dfd527.headline: Meeting recessed at 10:57 p.m.
17e40cd736dfd527.summary: The council recessed for the night at 10:57 p.m.
17e40cd736dfd527.impact: This is the clock stopping on a long agenda. Nobody outside the council chamber is touched by it.

18b41a4ed883bdf2.headline: Sign height now measured from natural grade
18b41a4ed883bdf2.summary: The city changed its sign rules so a sign's height is measured from the natural ground level rather than an altered one.
18b41a4ed883bdf2.impact: If you are putting up a sign, mostly businesses and developers, the allowed height is now measured from the original ground, so building up the dirt underneath will not buy extra height.

198d0d9c3de06305.headline: Five city advisory boards merged into one
198d0d9c3de06305.summary: The council dissolved the parks and recreation, recreation sports, cemetery, military and veterans, and economic development boards, replacing all five with a single Community Services Board.
198d0d9c3de06305.impact: If you volunteer on one of these boards, or bring ideas about parks, sports, the cemetery or veterans' affairs to them, there is now one board to go to instead of five.

19946c45c2fadb30.headline: School land transfer tied to replacing school site
19946c45c2fadb30.summary: The city agreed to a property transfer inside the new west county school district, on the condition that a replacement parcel is bought for the elementary school.
19946c45c2fadb30.impact: This matters to families waiting on the elementary school: the city's consent only holds if the district buys replacement land, so a site has to stay set aside for the school.

19e990beeef1819f.headline: Expired development deals now trigger rezoning
19e990beeef1819f.summary: The council required the planning director to start rezoning land whenever a master development agreement or development agreement on it expires or is terminated.
19e990beeef1819f.impact: If you own land covered by a development agreement that lapses, the city will move to rezone it rather than leave the old zoning in place. Most residents will not notice this.

19fdd9af77c0844d.headline: Amenity swap rules added to city's law wish list
19fdd9af77c0844d.summary: The council put a new rule on its legislative priorities list requiring developers to raise amenity exchange requests early in the approval process.
19fdd9af77c0844d.impact: Nothing changes yet: this only flags the idea for a future code change. Developers swapping one promised amenity for another would eventually have to ask sooner.

1aeb19e33a0fd005.headline: Rezone Eagle Mountain Properties land, mostly to farm
1aeb19e33a0fd005.summary: The council rezoned 27 parcels in the Eagle Mountain Properties plan area: most to agriculture, seven to neighborhood commercial, two to low-to-medium density housing.
1aeb19e33a0fd005.impact: Nothing changes on the ground now. The zoning sets what each parcel can become later, so people living near the seven commercial parcels are the ones with a reason to follow it.

1afc21853f708a71.headline: New code chapter covers city officer pay
1afc21853f708a71.summary: The council wrote a new chapter into city code, Chapter 2.20, setting the compensation schedule for Eagle Mountain's statutory officers.
1afc21853f708a71.impact: No dollar figures appear in the motion, so it does not tell you what any officer will be paid. Nothing you pay or receive changes.

1bcd71f6b39c0618.headline: Final zoning set for the White Hills area
1bcd71f6b39c0618.summary: The council assigned final zoning across the White Hills area, including one commercial lot, two agricultural parcels, and ten parcels set to rural agriculture.
1bcd71f6b39c0618.impact: If you own land in White Hills, this fixes what you may build there: most of it stays rural or farm land, with one parcel opened to neighborhood-scale commercial use.

1bd3b8d56f5dd862.headline: Zoning code definitions updated
1bd3b8d56f5dd862.summary: The council changed the wording of definitions in the city's zoning code, section 17.10.030. The motion does not say which terms changed.
1bd3b8d56f5dd862.impact: Definitions decide how the rest of the zoning rules get read, so anyone drawing up building plans may want to check the new wording. For most households this passes unnoticed.

1c188b116578f003.headline: SITLA land swap in Overland put on hold
1c188b116578f003.summary: The council set aside a decision on trading city property for state trust land in the Overland area, with no new date given.
1c188b116578f003.impact: Nothing changes on the ground while the swap waits. If you live near Overland, the land in question stays in the same hands until the council takes the item back up.

1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.headline: Sewer master plan and impact fee plan approved
1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.summary: The council approved the city's wastewater master plan and the impact fee facilities plan setting out which sewer projects new growth is expected to pay for.
1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.impact: Sewer service at existing homes doesn't change. The plan is the basis the city uses to charge impact fees on new construction, so it mainly touches builders and anyone building a new home here.

1caeedf39d59002d.headline: $20,000 added for a special events UTV
1caeedf39d59002d.summary: The council moved $20,000 into the Special Events budget line so staff could have more choice in which utility task vehicle to buy.
1caeedf39d59002d.impact: A small equipment purchase for the crews who run city events. You may see the vehicle at a city event; otherwise this passes you by.

1dc55f3b8940cb04.headline: Consent agenda approved
1dc55f3b8940cb04.summary: The council cleared its consent agenda, the batch of items handled together without separate discussion.
1dc55f3b8940cb04.impact: Consent items are the ones the council judged uncontroversial enough to pass in a single vote. The motion itself lists no specifics, so there is nothing here for a resident to act on.

1e54ecf0681505b1.headline: Council rules rewrite pushed to February
1e54ecf0681505b1.summary: The council put off an ordinance spelling out its six-member form of government and how a mayor pro tempore is chosen, sending it back for rewording.
1e54ecf0681505b1.impact: Nothing changes for you yet. The rules govern how councilmembers, staff and the mayor may speak for the city, and the reworked version was set to return on February 6.

1eccd0e76fdd7a74.headline: Water and sewer deal with Meta updated
1eccd0e76fdd7a74.summary: The council approved a third change to the water and sewer agreement with Stadion, LLC, the company known as Meta.
1eccd0e76fdd7a74.impact: This governs the water and sewer service the Meta site gets and on what terms. The motion doesn't say what the change does, so no effect on your household bill is stated.

1edbd9d357577106.headline: Spring Run Plaza approved on 27.35 acres
1edbd9d357577106.summary: The city approved the layout for Spring Run Plaza, a 27.35-acre development at Spring Run Parkway and Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway, starting with six lots.
1edbd9d357577106.impact: If you live or drive near that corner, expect construction on the first 8.15 acres. Two of the lots stay empty until the developer comes back to the city for approval.

1f4a5b99acc0b157.headline: Lot lines redrawn in Saddle Junction
1f4a5b99acc0b157.summary: The council approved an amended plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1, known as the Allgood plat amendment, redrawing the recorded lot layout.
1f4a5b99acc0b157.impact: This touches the property owner and immediate neighbors in Saddle Junction. If you live elsewhere in the city, it changes nothing for you.

1f8e71c45ed2046f.headline: Taller fences where businesses sit above homes
1f8e71c45ed2046f.summary: Fence height gets measured differently now: where a commercial or industrial pad sits above neighboring homes, the council set the taller screen as the standard.
1f8e71c45ed2046f.impact: If a business lot beside your yard is built up higher than your property, the screening fence is measured from that higher pad and blocks more. Only homes on those boundaries, and the builders next door, are touched.

1ffdeea4575c1804.headline: Gazelle Run application fee cut to $1,350
1ffdeea4575c1804.summary: The council cut the fee for Brett Simpson's Gazelle Run master development plan amendment from $3,350 to $1,350, rather than waiving it entirely as first proposed.
1ffdeea4575c1804.impact: This touches one applicant only. The city collects $2,000 less on this single application, and the fees everyone else pays are unchanged.

2014658e53ffc562.headline: Two zoning proposals dropped from lobbying list
2014658e53ffc562.summary: The council struck two items, on discontinued zoning and transfer of development rights ordinances, from its list of state legislative priorities.
2014658e53ffc562.impact: This trims what the city asks lawmakers to take up next session. Nothing changes on the ground for residents or property owners.

21312b65de4a2b35.headline: Sign rules now cover city fields and Rodeo Grounds
21312b65de4a2b35.summary: The council rewrote the city's sign rules and defined an "athletic facility" as a high school, middle school, or city-owned regulation field, or the Rodeo Grounds.
21312b65de4a2b35.impact: The sign rules that apply at athletic venues now reach city-owned fields and the Rodeo Grounds, not just school fields. For most residents, day-to-day life is unchanged.

2161b9b40d595a90.headline: Citywide speed study, paid for with speed table money
2161b9b40d595a90.summary: The city approved a citywide speed management study, added roads named by Councilmember Wood, and paid for it with money set aside for speed tables.
2161b9b40d595a90.impact: Money earmarked to build speed tables now buys the study instead, so any street waiting on one waits on this first. The study looks at speeds across the whole city.

218f010d801a8378.headline: Golf course noise allowed to start at 5:30 a.m.
218f010d801a8378.summary: The council changed the city's noise rules so golf course maintenance noise is restricted only between 10 p.m. and 5:30 a.m.
218f010d801a8378.impact: If you live near the golf course, crews can legally start mowing and maintenance at 5:30 in the morning. Everyone else sees no change.

22db0b6251bc32f7.headline: Bid to pause the land sale turned down
22db0b6251bc32f7.summary: Council members declined to hold off on the land sale while staff tightened water requirements and wrote a policy for reviewing future purchase requests.
22db0b6251bc32f7.impact: A postponement that does not happen leaves nothing for you to notice. The sale itself was decided in a separate vote.

239f7e55bff45b15.headline: Consent agenda approved
239f7e55bff45b15.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together without separate discussion; the motion does not list what was included.
239f7e55bff45b15.impact: Nothing here changes for residents on its own. The individual items are listed on the meeting agenda.

24b230adfee0fd6c.headline: Sewer easement released on one property
24b230adfee0fd6c.summary: The council gave up a permanent sewer easement across a property while keeping a temporary one in place.
24b230adfee0fd6c.impact: This frees up land the city no longer needs a permanent sewer line through. It affects that one property owner, nobody else.

25d8c9c542583d2b.headline: Bid to keep 15 acres commercial went nowhere
25d8c9c542583d2b.summary: The council took no action on an alternative version of the land use change that would have preserved roughly 15 acres of commercial land near SR-73 and Airport Road.
25d8c9c542583d2b.impact: Nothing follows from this item on its own: the council adopted the version that converts the full 73 acres, so no commercial land was carved out near the SR-73 and Airport Road intersection.

2775ed0d599459dc.headline: Consent agenda approved
2775ed0d599459dc.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote, covering the routine items grouped there.
2775ed0d599459dc.impact: Consent items are the ones no councilmember flagged for discussion. Nothing here reaches your street or your bill.

279499360546d485.headline: Four items pulled off the consent list
279499360546d485.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, dropping one from the agenda and pulling three others out for discussion instead.
279499360546d485.impact: A scheduling move that decided which items got debated in the open rather than passed in a block. The items themselves were decided separately.

2895e8e0ec99fd85.headline: New map of land the city could annex
2895e8e0ec99fd85.summary: The council updated the city's annexation policy plan, extending Area 1 to Utah Lake and dropping language about SITLA and Saratoga Springs from the response to other agencies.
2895e8e0ec99fd85.impact: The map marks land Eagle Mountain would consider taking in. Owners of unincorporated property near the edges may now have a choice of which city to join. Nothing changes inside current city limits.

29bbb5872984a679.headline: Fewer parking spaces required for hotels
29bbb5872984a679.summary: The council changed the city code's parking rules for hotels, motels and bed-and-breakfast businesses, altering how many spaces those buildings must provide.
29bbb5872984a679.impact: This lands on anyone planning or building lodging in Eagle Mountain. If you are not putting up a hotel, nothing in your day changes.

2babc3a20cfdf239.headline: Inland port project area rejected
2babc3a20cfdf239.summary: The council turned down a resolution backing a Utah Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain.
2babc3a20cfdf239.impact: An inland port district will not move forward here with the council's blessing. Residents near any proposed industrial site keep the status quo.

2bfff6eede2b2165.headline: Jay Johnson gets a one-year board term
2bfff6eede2b2165.summary: The council appointed Jay Johnson to a one-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2027.
2bfff6eede2b2165.impact: The shortest of the terms handed out that night, and the last seat filled. Nobody outside the board is touched by it.

2c6a2c4dbab14a2d.headline: Triumph subdivision deal adds 53 affordable homes
2c6a2c4dbab14a2d.summary: The council approved a revised Triumph development agreement covering 53 units in one section of Plat 2, with fencing, water-wise landscaping and full appliances required.
2c6a2c4dbab14a2d.impact: If you're buying in the Triumph subdivision, the affordable homes in that pod must be owner-occupied and come with appliances and landscaping included. Water-rate help for the project lasts only while redevelopment funds hold out.

2c7564b1969f48a5.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
2c7564b1969f48a5.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in one vote after pulling items 12.G and 12.H off the list.
2c7564b1969f48a5.impact: Consent items are the ones the council treats as uncontested and passes together. The two pulled items were dropped from the evening's business.

2e17bbe3fdad07d1.headline: Brandon Park area given formal zoning
2e17bbe3fdad07d1.summary: The council put official zoning designations on the Brandon Park area, updating both the city zoning map and the future land use map.
2e17bbe3fdad07d1.impact: Property owners in and around Brandon Park now have a zoning label on record that governs what can be built there. The motion names no change in allowed uses.

2e974bec4ca19318.headline: Wildlife corridor rules held for rewrites
2e974bec4ca19318.summary: A vote on updated wildlife corridor overlay rules was put off by the council until staff makes the changes members asked for.
2e974bec4ca19318.impact: Landowners inside the corridor keep building under today's rules until the item returns. Questions raised about fencing around livestock and setbacks from washes stay unsettled.

2f9f38315e99c875.headline: Meeting capped at 10:30 PM
2f9f38315e99c875.summary: The council set 10:30 PM as the end time for the December 3 meeting.
2f9f38315e99c875.impact: A scheduling call for the people in the room that night. It touches nobody outside the council chamber.

30068fa852d9b8c2.headline: Meta site road narrowed and redesigned
30068fa852d9b8c2.summary: The city approved a revised street design at the META site, shrinking the sidewalk from 8 feet to 5 and turning the parking lane into a 12-foot drive lane.
30068fa852d9b8c2.impact: If you walk or drive near the META site, the sidewalk will be narrower than originally planned and there will be no on-street parking lane. The 8-foot grass strip becomes a drainage swale instead.

30bf97e474e194dc.headline: Wording fixed on the tax remittance deal
30bf97e474e194dc.summary: The council took up the collection agreement for the Mid-Valley project area, and the city attorney corrected the agenda, which said property tax where it should have said sales tax.
30bf97e474e194dc.impact: A drafting error caught on the record, and the record shows no vote on this version. Your tax bill is untouched by a spelling correction.

30ffb0a57e413f3c.headline: City manager finalists picked for interviews
30ffb0a57e413f3c.summary: The council settled on the shortlist of city manager candidates it will interview, drawn from names put forward by the recruiting firm handling the search.
30ffb0a57e413f3c.impact: The city manager runs day to day operations, so the eventual hire matters, but this step only decides who gets an interview. Nothing reaches you until the council picks someone.

3245d5fe1c278c4a.headline: Emily Buss joins the Library Advisory Board
3245d5fe1c278c4a.summary: The council appointed Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board to finish a three-year term running through December 2027.
3245d5fe1c278c4a.impact: The board advises on library matters. Filling the seat has no effect on hours, fees, or services you use.

329c1ff8627a8c53.headline: City property tax revenue up 69.81%
329c1ff8627a8c53.summary: The council set the property tax rate at 0.000900, above the certified rate of 0.000530, raising city property tax revenue about $2.13 million, or 69.81%, over last year.
329c1ff8627a8c53.impact: If you own property in Eagle Mountain, the city share of your next bill goes up. That 69.81% counts existing property only, so new homes being built does not explain it.

3301b51649590e11.headline: Noise rule change pulled before a vote
3301b51649590e11.summary: A proposed rewrite of the city's noise limits was put forward and then withdrawn, so the existing rule stands unchanged.
3301b51649590e11.impact: The noise limits that applied to your neighborhood last week still apply. Whether the council takes the rewrite up again is not recorded here.

345d6cd48ceee0d2.headline: Lot lines redrawn in Rush Creek industrial area
345d6cd48ceee0d2.summary: The council approved changes to two lots, 102 and 111, in Phase A of the Rush Creek Industrial plat.
345d6cd48ceee0d2.impact: This is a boundary change on paper in an industrial area. It affects the property owner and what can be built on those two lots, not the average resident.

3523e2a88ea7f0a0.headline: Job offer made to a new city manager
3523e2a88ea7f0a0.summary: The council voted to offer the city manager job to its chosen candidate and sent the mayor and Councilmember Wright to negotiate the employment contract.
3523e2a88ea7f0a0.impact: The city manager runs day-to-day operations, from budgets to staffing. You will not deal with this person directly, but the terms of the contract, including pay, come back to the council before anything is final.

354136822e2f1afe.headline: Pacific Springs development agreement approved
354136822e2f1afe.summary: The council approved a development agreement for Pacific Springs, the contract setting the terms under which that project can be built.
354136822e2f1afe.impact: The motion itself does not spell out the size, location, or number of homes, so the specifics are in the agreement rather than the vote. It clears the way for the Pacific Springs project to move forward.

3789dc39e9e73310.headline: City land to be sold at $3.44 a square foot
3789dc39e9e73310.summary: The council approved selling a significant piece of city-owned land at $3.44 per square foot, with staff directed to work out the financing terms.
3789dc39e9e73310.impact: The price is set, but the motion does not name the property or the buyer, so what eventually gets built there is still unknown. Staff still has to settle how the buyer pays.

37fb3507f124cf7f.headline: Dani McKean joins Library Advisory Board
37fb3507f124cf7f.summary: The council appointed Dani McKean to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.
37fb3507f124cf7f.impact: Library board members advise on the library. Filling the seat changes nothing about hours, cards or fees.

3804516bb044944b.headline: City Center lot rezoned to neighborhood commercial
3804516bb044944b.summary: The council rezoned Plat 1 of City Center Commercial Phase A from Commercial C-1 to Commercial Neighborhood, picked over a broader zone after concerns about allowed uses.
3804516bb044944b.impact: What can open on that ground is now governed by the Commercial Neighborhood list, which councilmembers preferred to the wider Commercial Community zone. Households next to the site have the stake here.

38555386e56b9873.headline: Consent items approved, one pulled
38555386e56b9873.summary: The council approved its batch of consent items, recorded a change order at $47,930, and pulled item 15.C so no action was taken on it.
38555386e56b9873.impact: These are the items grouped together because none of them needed debate. The pulled item stays undecided until the council brings it back.

3906b550937e078f.headline: Mandy Lane appointed planning commissioner
3906b550937e078f.summary: Mandy Lane was appointed to the Planning Commission for a one-year term through December 2026.
3906b550937e078f.impact: The Planning Commission reviews zoning and development proposals before they reach the council. Her seat comes up again at the end of the year.

39890370d9c12d21.headline: Consent agenda approved
39890370d9c12d21.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together in a single vote; the motion does not list what was included.
39890370d9c12d21.impact: Routine housekeeping. Nothing here changes for residents.

3a02fa5f88f3a3c2.headline: New Alpine School District elementary school approved
3a02fa5f88f3a3c2.summary: The council approved the preliminary plat and site plan for Alpine School District's Elementary 133.
3a02fa5f88f3a3c2.impact: If you live near the site, expect school construction and eventually the traffic a new elementary school brings. This approval clears the way for the district to build.

3bce390e7d1deb27.headline: Ten-year deal for ShopFest Utah event
3bce390e7d1deb27.summary: The city signed an agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce to host the ShopFest Utah event, stretching the term to ten years, through 2035.
3bce390e7d1deb27.impact: ShopFest is now locked in as a recurring local event through 2035. The rest of the changes are contract wording between the city and the chamber, and you will not notice them.

3c545a81a8995e46.headline: Seventh change to last year's city budget
3c545a81a8995e46.summary: The council adopted the seventh amendment to the 2024-2025 city budget, adjusting spending figures before the fiscal year closed.
3c545a81a8995e46.impact: Year-end budget cleanup at city hall. The motion names no project or dollar figure, so there is nothing here you would notice.

3c6cb58d5286dd0d.headline: Rose Ranch development agreement fails
3c6cb58d5286dd0d.summary: A master development agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision was put forward but never taken up by the council.
3c6cb58d5286dd0d.impact: No other councilmember backed the motion, so Rose Ranch has no approved development agreement. Anyone watching that subdivision is back where they started.

3d6b7573482e9255.headline: Cedar Corners land use map change delayed
3d6b7573482e9255.summary: A change to the general plan's future land use map covering Cedar Corners Phase 5 was delayed, with the public hearing continued.
3d6b7573482e9255.impact: This is the companion piece to the zoning item on the same ground, and it waits with it. Neighbors keep their chance to comment at a later meeting.

3f5d7595a2cbb27c.headline: Sweetwater #4 redevelopment plan adopted
3f5d7595a2cbb27c.summary: The council adopted the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area plan as the official plan governing redevelopment in that project area.
3f5d7595a2cbb27c.impact: If you live or own property near Sweetwater #4, this sets the framework for what gets built there and how tax revenue from that growth is reinvested. The motion names no dollar amounts or timeline.

3fb75c7fc7a85b20.headline: Easement rules sent back for rewrite
3fb75c7fc7a85b20.summary: The council delayed new rules on easements until November 6, asking the city attorney to define "conservation easement" and to give the Planning Commission approval power over those, with golf course easements staying with the council.
3fb75c7fc7a85b20.impact: Property owners and developers dealing with easements keep the current rules for now. The change would decide which body signs off on an easement crossing your land.

4015c65a5ef4ad2a.headline: Third change to this year's city budget
4015c65a5ef4ad2a.summary: The council approved a third amendment to the 2025-2026 budget, adjusting the city's spending plan for the fiscal year now ending.
4015c65a5ef4ad2a.impact: The motion doesn't say what was moved or added, so no change to your bills or services is stated. This is the city squaring its books before the year closes.

413db5ca042fc3c5.headline: Ivory Homes agreement approved, water break cut
413db5ca042fc3c5.summary: The city approved an agreement with builder Ivory Homes but removed a proposed break on per-lot water requirements and downgraded promised city benefits to something it "may" consider.
413db5ca042fc3c5.impact: Ivory Homes will have to meet the city's normal water requirement for each lot rather than a reduced one, and any city incentives are now optional rather than guaranteed.

4155fa5e631dc0e5.headline: Jessi Call named Youth Council advisor
4155fa5e631dc0e5.summary: The council appointed Jessi Call as an advisor to the Youth Council Committee, effective immediately and running through June 30, 2026.
4155fa5e631dc0e5.impact: Families with teens in the Youth Council will see a new advisor. For everyone else, this one changes nothing.

4179c6403f0edf66.headline: Mid-year budget update approved
4179c6403f0edf66.summary: The council approved a second round of amendments to the city's 2025–26 budget; the motion itself names no specific dollar figures.
4179c6403f0edf66.impact: Cities adjust their budgets partway through the year to match actual spending. Nothing in this motion spells out a change residents would notice: the detail sits in the budget document, not the motion.

4233dd274c2fa68c.headline: Job offer made for city manager
4233dd274c2fa68c.summary: The council voted to offer the city manager job to its chosen candidate and let the mayor work out the pay and terms.
4233dd274c2fa68c.impact: The city manager runs day-to-day operations, so this shapes who answers when you call about a permit or a pothole. Nothing changes for you until a contract is signed.

4306735e032f07e3.headline: Porter's Crossing development deal amended
4306735e032f07e3.summary: The council approved a fourth amendment to the master development agreement governing the Porter's Crossing project.
4306735e032f07e3.impact: This changes the terms the city and the developer agreed to for Porter's Crossing. It matters most to people living in or buying near that development; the rest of the city sees no direct change.

43305ee3d9ddd2cb.headline: Pinnacles B-3 site plan put on hold
43305ee3d9ddd2cb.summary: The council set the master site plan for Pinnacles B-3 aside without deciding it.
43305ee3d9ddd2cb.impact: Nothing is settled either way. The plan can come back to the council later. If you live near the Pinnacles area, this only delays the decision.

433adac40200ac3d.headline: Update road right-of-way drawings in city code
433adac40200ac3d.summary: The council amended the city's code section covering the illustrations that show how streets and the land beside them must be laid out.
433adac40200ac3d.impact: Engineers and developers drawing up new streets work from these diagrams. For everyone else it is a technical drawing swap with nothing to see.

43a6c4ed57a84083.headline: Noise and property nuisance rules rewritten
43a6c4ed57a84083.summary: The council approved changes to the city's nuisance abatement and noise rules, though the motion itself does not spell out what was changed.
43a6c4ed57a84083.impact: These are the rules behind noise complaints and property-upkeep enforcement, so they apply citywide. The motion text doesn't say what changed. Read the ordinance before assuming your yard or late-night habits are affected.

43f635c99de0552f.headline: Change how contract change orders get approved
43f635c99de0552f.summary: The council rewrote the purchasing rules to change who signs off when the cost or scope of a city contract changes mid-project.
43f635c99de0552f.impact: An internal spending control that lives inside city hall. You will not run into it unless you hold a contract with the city.

44fd40041700b17d.headline: Hidden Hollow amenity swap approved
44fd40041700b17d.summary: The city approved a site plan letting the Hidden Hollow development swap amenities for a wellness center, outdoor gathering area, and new fitness equipment.
44fd40041700b17d.impact: If you live in Hidden Hollow, the amenities your neighborhood gets are changing, and the clubhouse must still include at least one amenity. The final terms come back to the council in a written agreement.

4502d3e94a0029a3.headline: Subdivision plat rules amended
4502d3e94a0029a3.summary: The council amended the city's rules for preliminary and final plats, the approval steps land must clear before it can be split into lots.
4502d3e94a0029a3.impact: This changes the process for developers and anyone subdividing land; the motion does not spell out what the new rules require. Existing homeowners see no change.

4718a702504a2186.headline: City to study accepting bitcoin for payments
4718a702504a2186.summary: The council added a study of bitcoin as a way to pay the city to its list of legislative priorities.
4718a702504a2186.impact: Nothing changes at the utility billing counter for now. This puts the question on a list to look into, not into practice.

47509f94ec3c8f9b.headline: Political sign rules rewritten
47509f94ec3c8f9b.summary: The council amended the section of the city code that governs political signs; the motion itself does not spell out what the new rules say.
47509f94ec3c8f9b.impact: The rules for putting campaign signs on your own property have changed. If you plan to post signs before an election, check the city's updated sign code rather than assuming the old limits still apply.

48096f2ab8755f8e.headline: Benjamin Perez joins the library board
48096f2ab8755f8e.summary: Benjamin Perez was appointed to a three year term on the Library Advisory Board, running through 2027.
48096f2ab8755f8e.impact: The board advises on library matters. Unless you go to those meetings, this one passes you by.

490e074e93a80f98.headline: Land use map updated for Berry property
490e074e93a80f98.summary: The council took up a matching change to the general plan land use map for the Berry property.
490e074e93a80f98.impact: This is the paperwork that lines the city's long-range map up with the zoning change on the same land. On its own, it changes nothing you would see.

4b2259a946011f33.headline: City sells 0.156 acres to neighboring property owners
4b2259a946011f33.summary: The council approved disposing of 0.156 acres of city-owned land, gave the buyers a year to finish, and dropped one lot from the deal.
4b2259a946011f33.impact: This touches only the handful of adjoining property owners in the agreement, who now have a year to complete the transfer. One lot no longer has to take part.

4b5e019b19bb4021.headline: City website contract change order approved
4b5e019b19bb4021.summary: The council approved a change order to its website contract with WDG, rewriting the cost language so the vendor can adjust for unforeseen variables.
4b5e019b19bb4021.impact: Work continues on the city's website. The rewritten clause is a matter between the city and its vendor, and you will not notice it.

4b9e8c485db5c455.headline: Emily Hoehne joins Library Advisory Board
4b9e8c485db5c455.summary: The council appointed Emily Hoehne to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.
4b9e8c485db5c455.impact: Another volunteer seat filled on the board that advises the library. Nobody's day changes because of it.

4bb68f5b877246cc.headline: Street width and sidewalk rules put on hold
4bb68f5b877246cc.summary: The council delayed a decision on updated street cross-section rules, asking staff to return with recommendations on curb, gutter and a sidewalk for rural 50-foot streets.
4bb68f5b877246cc.impact: No change yet. Whatever the council settles on would shape how new streets are built: mainly affecting new subdivisions, not existing ones.

4bb8bb8ec80f51c7.headline: Sewer plant expansion contract awarded
4bb8bb8ec80f51c7.summary: The council awarded MGC Contractors the job of building the oxidation ditch and related site work for expanding the city sewer plant to 6 million gallons a day.
4bb8bb8ec80f51c7.impact: The plant that treats what goes down your drain gets bigger, which is what lets the city keep connecting new homes. No price appears in the motion.

4bc107d10a726322.headline: New rules for fences and screening
4bc107d10a726322.summary: The council rewrote the section of city code covering general fencing and screening, changing the rules that apply when property owners put up a fence or wall.
4bc107d10a726322.impact: If you are planning a fence at your home or business, check the updated code before you build. The requirements are not the same as they were.

4be32b7d4441caa0.headline: Sign rules rewrite delayed
4be32b7d4441caa0.summary: The council shelved proposed changes to the city's sign rules and permit requirements without voting on them.
4be32b7d4441caa0.impact: The existing sign rules stay in force, so businesses and homeowners follow the same permit requirements as before until the council takes the item back up.

4bebdd2be34824da.headline: New school district proposal approved
4bebdd2be34824da.summary: The council approved the proposal to create a new school district and set the date for its final decision on it.
4bebdd2be34824da.impact: This advances the proposal rather than settling it; a final council vote is still to come. If a new district is created, it would change which school district Eagle Mountain belongs to.

4ccee4d22e0cbf66.headline: City brand and marketing playbook adopted
4ccee4d22e0cbf66.summary: The council adopted the city's brand and market playbook and asked for it to return at a later meeting once the additions raised in discussion are written in.
4ccee4d22e0cbf66.impact: Signs, letterhead and city messaging follow from this document. No resident is asked to do anything.

4cd08b477b5827cf.headline: Consent agenda approved with a minutes fix
4cd08b477b5827cf.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after correcting a spelling error in the minutes of the January 6, 2026 meeting.
4cd08b477b5827cf.impact: Housekeeping from start to finish. One misspelled word in the record of an earlier meeting was the whole of it.

4d14b944f63eedc1.headline: Water and sewer rate changes taken up
4d14b944f63eedc1.summary: The council took up changes to the city's fee schedule for water rates, sewer rates, and utility billing; the record does not show a final outcome.
4d14b944f63eedc1.impact: This is the schedule that sets what you pay on your monthly water and sewer bill. The motion itself does not say how the rates would change, and the record does not show whether it was adopted.

4db177b4f1537563.headline: Rules changed for building into yard setbacks
4db177b4f1537563.summary: The council amended the city code rule governing how far a structure may project into a required yard setback.
4db177b4f1537563.impact: If you are planning to build near your property line, the limits on how far a structure can extend into the setback have changed. The motion itself does not state the new limits, so check with the city first.

4f091bf6f56af544.headline: 178 acres proposed for Pole Canyon district
4f091bf6f56af544.summary: The council took up a resolution consenting to the annexation of 178 acres of land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District.
4f091bf6f56af544.impact: This concerns the 178 acres in question and which district serves them, not existing neighborhoods. The meeting record does not show how this one ended.

4f1859ee1a28f9aa.headline: Meeting extended to 12:30 a.m.
4f1859ee1a28f9aa.summary: The council gave itself until 12:30 in the morning to finish the night's business.
4f1859ee1a28f9aa.impact: Anyone watching at home sat through a long one. No rule, rate or project moved because of it.

4f8e82fc4e9e9f1c.headline: Recycling use sent back for a rewrite
4f8e82fc4e9e9f1c.summary: The council turned down changes to zoning definitions, conditional uses and land use tables, and asked staff to return with the recycling piece as a special use.
4f8e82fc4e9e9f1c.impact: Nothing in the zoning code changed today. The recycling part comes back to the council later as a special use; the rest of the proposal is off the table.

5022c0d008fb4a68.headline: General plan change for the same land denied
5022c0d008fb4a68.summary: Alongside the zoning refusal, the council declined to change the general plan for the same parcels from community commercial and civic uses to neighborhood residential.
5022c0d008fb4a68.impact: The city's long-range map still shows commercial and civic use for this ground. A housing-only project there would need a fresh application and a fresh argument.

505321d714b5a33c.headline: Hiring process set for a new city administrator
505321d714b5a33c.summary: Council members adopted a process for hiring a permanent city administrator, following the recruitment handbook of the national city and county managers' association.
505321d714b5a33c.impact: This sets the rules the city follows while it recruits. Nothing here reaches a resident.

510cf9e86add9230.headline: Steve Mumford named interim city administrator
510cf9e86add9230.summary: Steve Mumford was appointed interim city administrator, the staff job that runs the city's day-to-day operations, on a temporary basis.
510cf9e86add9230.impact: City Hall has someone in charge again. You deal with the same offices and the same counter staff as before.

5152efc76543036a.headline: Long-range land use map updated for Big Eagle 7
5152efc76543036a.summary: The council amended the General Plan's future land use map for the land known as Big Eagle 7.
5152efc76543036a.impact: The General Plan is the city's long-term blueprint for what goes where. This redraws that map for the Big Eagle 7 area; nothing on the ground changes immediately.

5193039e0cf72edb.headline: 2024 board liaison assignments set
5193039e0cf72edb.summary: The council handed each member board assignments for the year, from the cemetery and arts boards to the Planning Commission and the Utah League of Cities and Towns.
5193039e0cf72edb.impact: If you sit on one of those boards, you now know which councilmember will be in the room with you. For everyone else this is an internal calendar.

51d7e3eb20aea2aa.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 development deal approved
51d7e3eb20aea2aa.summary: The city approved a development agreement for Cedar Corners Phase 5, with conditions on when construction may start and on connecting the roads and sidewalks.
51d7e3eb20aea2aa.impact: If you live near Poplar Drive or Maple Street, the developer must connect the roads on both sides and keep the walkways continuous rather than leaving them to dead-end.

51ea4965b8e28a32.headline: Property tax increase heads to a hearing
51ea4965b8e28a32.summary: The council took up a resolution declaring the city's intent to raise property tax revenue, give public notice, and set the required Truth-in-Taxation hearing date.
51ea4965b8e28a32.impact: If the increase goes ahead, homeowners would pay more. The Truth-in-Taxation hearing is the point where you can speak before the council settles on a final rate.

524eaaf50b91ac01.headline: Three items pulled for open discussion
524eaaf50b91ac01.summary: The council pulled the Eagle Square plat, a wayfinding sign agreement and the marketing contract off the consent list so each got its own debate.
524eaaf50b91ac01.impact: You will not feel this directly, but it meant three spending and development items were argued in public rather than passed in a single vote.

532ed6460234c068.headline: Fence rule changes put on hold
532ed6460234c068.summary: The council set aside proposed changes to the city's fencing rules and sent them back for a future work session.
532ed6460234c068.impact: Current fence rules stay in place. If you were waiting to see whether the limits on your fence would change, the answer is not yet.

538d097678f79cb6.headline: Porter's Crossing lot rezoned from open space to housing
538d097678f79cb6.summary: The council rezoned one lot in Porter's Crossing from open space to R1, the city's single-family housing zone.
538d097678f79cb6.impact: A parcel that was set aside as open space can now hold a house. If you live next to that lot in Porter's Crossing, expect a home there instead of undeveloped ground.

53ad04727b025886.headline: Consent agenda passed, two items pulled
53ad04727b025886.summary: The council passed its consent agenda covering a right-of-way land purchase, arena equipment, two bond releases, February minutes and two treasurer appointments, pulling two items out.
53ad04727b025886.impact: Housekeeping cleared in a single vote. The two items lifted out, including the recruitment consultants' contract, went to open discussion later in the evening.

54e5838afc15ab7b.headline: Water plan added to the city General Plan
54e5838afc15ab7b.summary: A Water Use and Preservation Plan became an official appendix to Eagle Mountain's 2018 General Plan.
54e5838afc15ab7b.impact: The city now has an adopted policy document to point to on water use and conservation. Nothing in the motion changes your water bill or watering rules today.

54f80eaa76e263d7.headline: City land sold at $2.07 a square foot
54f80eaa76e263d7.summary: The city approved selling part of a city-owned parcel in Utah County at $2.07 per square foot, with the buyer paying all related costs.
54f80eaa76e263d7.impact: Most residents will notice nothing. The buyer covers the survey and other fees, so the sale costs the city nothing and moves a piece of public land into private hands.

5540a62cc4c397eb.headline: Four items pulled for separate discussion
5540a62cc4c397eb.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling four items out for full discussion later in the meeting.
5540a62cc4c397eb.impact: Nothing was decided here beyond the order of business. The four pulled items got their own debate instead of passing in a batch.

556b6e9e5b47cb85.headline: Mayor's powers ordinance tabled
556b6e9e5b47cb85.summary: A proposed rewrite of the code section listing the mayor's powers and duties was set aside, leaving the existing version in place.
556b6e9e5b47cb85.impact: The mayor's job description is unchanged. This one is watched at city hall and nowhere else.

55974898ac3a2e40.headline: Elizabeth Evans joins Community Services Board
55974898ac3a2e40.summary: The council appointed Elizabeth Evans to the Community Services Board for a one-year term ending March 2027.
55974898ac3a2e40.impact: One more volunteer seat filled on an advisory board. No service, fee, or rule changes because of it.

560b169a35ad1ebf.headline: Consent items approved, one pulled and a vote count fixed
560b169a35ad1ebf.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulled item 13.A for a later meeting, and corrected the December 16 minutes to show a 3-0 vote instead of 3-2.
560b169a35ad1ebf.impact: Bookkeeping on the written record, plus one item pushed to a future agenda. Nobody outside the clerk's office feels this.

5695a6d9110c0094.headline: Drop ADU impact fee item from state lobbying list
5695a6d9110c0094.summary: The council struck the item on impact fees for accessory dwelling units from the list of priorities it takes to state lawmakers.
5695a6d9110c0094.impact: This shortens a wish list the city carries to the Legislature. Nothing changes today for homeowners weighing a basement or backyard apartment.

57c05393cf0231a9.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled
57c05393cf0231a9.summary: Everything on the consent agenda passed in a single vote except item 14.A, which the council moved to scheduled items for its own discussion.
57c05393cf0231a9.impact: Batching uncontroversial items into one vote is how the council saves floor time. The step touches nobody outside the meeting room.

57f21752fea7182a.headline: Mid-year budget adjustment
57f21752fea7182a.summary: The city made its fourth round of adjustments to the 2024-2025 budget.
57f21752fea7182a.impact: This is the mid-year bookkeeping the city does to true up its budget. The motion doesn't say which line items moved or by how much, so nothing here points to a change you would notice.

5936c4caca332e82.headline: Land rezoned for the new elementary school
5936c4caca332e82.summary: The council rezoned the land for Alpine School District's Elementary 133 so the school can be built there.
5936c4caca332e82.impact: Paired with the site plan approval, this lets the school district move ahead. Neighbors will get a school on that land instead of whatever the previous zoning allowed.

59b6a42a3fe950c7.headline: Less water required from builders per lot
59b6a42a3fe950c7.summary: The council cut the water a builder must hand the city per lot, dropping the indoor share from 0.53 to 0.34 acre-feet, and ordered a study of apartment water use.
59b6a42a3fe950c7.impact: Builders dedicating water rights for new subdivisions now hand over less, matching the smaller lawns the city already requires. Your own bill and service stay the same. The apartment study may bring the question back.

5a3d6e06075bce86.headline: Building standards for homes updated
5a3d6e06075bce86.summary: The council changed the city code's definition of a "structure" and its residential development standards table.
5a3d6e06075bce86.impact: If you are planning to build on your lot, the rules for what counts as a structure and the standards your project must meet have shifted. The motion itself doesn't spell out the specifics.

5a71a5e9f46f3f42.headline: April named Financial Literacy Month
5a71a5e9f46f3f42.summary: The council declared April 2025 Financial Literacy Month in Eagle Mountain.
5a71a5e9f46f3f42.impact: A symbolic declaration with no money or rules attached. Nothing is required of you.

5a862c799932541e.headline: Wildfire-risk map adopted for the city
5a862c799932541e.summary: The city adopted an official map of the areas where homes sit against wildland fire risk, and updated the related code chapter that governs them.
5a862c799932541e.impact: If your property falls inside the mapped wildland interface area, the city's Chapter 15.95 rules apply to it. The map is what decides whether you are in or out of that zone.

5af4b66ae66d70d0.headline: Backyard animal rules sent back for more work
5af4b66ae66d70d0.summary: The council sent proposed rules on alternative animal management plans, and the related zoning changes, back to the Planning Commission for further review.
5af4b66ae66d70d0.impact: Nothing changes for you yet. If you keep animals on your property, or want to, the rules stay as they are until the Planning Commission finishes its review and the council takes it up again.

5bd1eae88ffc55e4.headline: Fence rules rewritten, including chain link
5bd1eae88ffc55e4.summary: The council took up changes to the city's fence rules, covering definitions, privacy fencing, general fencing standards, and chain link fencing.
5bd1eae88ffc55e4.impact: Fence rules govern what you can put up around your own yard. The motion does not spell out what changed, so check the current code with the city before building a fence.

5bf4beb5c8a68ccd.headline: Bid to postpone the energy zone
5bf4beb5c8a68ccd.summary: Before deciding on the alternative energy overlay zone, the council considered setting it aside for a later meeting instead.
5bf4beb5c8a68ccd.impact: Jockeying over timing, nothing more. What reaches you is the zone decision itself, taken the same evening.

5c36ec68d1455668.headline: Consent agenda approved
5c36ec68d1455668.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the group of items passed together in one vote. The record here does not list which items were in the group.
5c36ec68d1455668.impact: With no list of items in the record, nothing here names a street, a fee, or a property. Nobody needs to do anything.

5c7179c232e1bd11.headline: Overland development change delayed
5c7179c232e1bd11.summary: The council postponed the fifth amendment to the Overland master development agreement and will take it up at a later meeting.
5c7179c232e1bd11.impact: Terms for building out Overland stay as they are for now. If you live near it or are following what gets built there, the decision is still open.

5d416daeb9ba7649.headline: MHTN Architects hired to plan downtown
5d416daeb9ba7649.summary: The council hired MHTN Architects to write the Downtown Master Plan, choosing the firm after hearing pitches from three competitors.
5d416daeb9ba7649.impact: A consultant will now draw up what a downtown Eagle Mountain could look like. Expect public input sessions before anything is built; no ground breaks on this contract.

5d49dfe012c02128.headline: Council starts property tax increase process
5d49dfe012c02128.summary: The council formally acknowledged the budget officer's statement that a property tax increase is proposed, along with the schedule of its impact on taxpayers.
5d49dfe012c02128.impact: This is the step Utah law requires before a city can raise property taxes, and it opens the Truth-in-Taxation process that leads to a public hearing. No rate was set here.

5d510b7d1c66c4b0.headline: Setback measuring rules left unsettled
5d510b7d1c66c4b0.summary: The council delayed a code change that would measure site plan distances from the existing right-of-way rather than the existing curb, with a diagram added for clarity.
5d510b7d1c66c4b0.impact: Nothing changes for now. When it returns, it will matter to anyone drawing up a site plan for a commercial or residential project, and to nobody else.

5e74fce9df30e88f.headline: Zayo Group gets a city franchise agreement
5e74fce9df30e88f.summary: Eagle Mountain approved a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, LLC, the second telecom deal the council passed that night.
5e74fce9df30e88f.impact: A company-and-city arrangement, not a change to anyone's internet service. The record of this motion does not say what Zayo will build or when.

5f372549b4f7a41d.headline: Angeline Washburn named Youth Council advisor
5f372549b4f7a41d.summary: The council appointed Angeline Washburn as an advisor to the Youth City Council, with a term running through May 31, 2027.
5f372549b4f7a41d.impact: This one reaches the Youth City Council and the volunteers around it. For everyone else in the city, nothing changes.

5fb5011ae1896332.headline: Fifth change to this year's city budget
5fb5011ae1896332.summary: The council approved the fifth amendment to the 2024-2025 city budget, shifting spending inside the current fiscal year.
5fb5011ae1896332.impact: The motion names no dollar figure or department, so there is no specific change a resident would feel from it. This is the city truing up its books mid-year.

5fc15cb5f1f35b35.headline: Hidden Hollow amenity swap put on hold
5fc15cb5f1f35b35.summary: The council delayed a decision on a minor change to the amenities planned for the Hidden Hollow development.
5fc15cb5f1f35b35.impact: If you live in or are buying into Hidden Hollow, the proposed change to the development's amenities is still unsettled and will come back to the council later.

6015205d292e2355.headline: Push for a youth court and justice court
6015205d292e2355.summary: The council added a youth court, a justice court and other public safety measures to the city's legislative priorities list, to be discussed with public safety partners and the Public Safety Director.
6015205d292e2355.impact: Nothing changes yet. This puts the idea on the city's wish list for talks with its public safety partners; any actual court would need separate decisions later.

602453a88b2b3bf1.headline: RAP tax question goes to voters in November
602453a88b2b3bf1.summary: The council put a 0.1% sales tax for recreation, arts, and cultural facilities on the November 4, 2025 ballot.
602453a88b2b3bf1.impact: You decide this one at the polls. If it passes, you would pay an extra 10 cents on every $100 spent in the city, with the money going to recreation and cultural facilities.

607b97fa29efc741.headline: Lot size rules sent back to staff
607b97fa29efc741.summary: The council delayed changes to lot size mixture and residential development standards, sending staff to collect councilmember feedback before a March 6 return.
607b97fa29efc741.impact: Builders waiting on the new lot rules wait another month. Anyone with an opinion on lot sizes gets another chance to speak when the item comes back March 6.

607b9c8ee0b238e7.headline: Push for Airport Road corridor funding at the Legislature
607b9c8ee0b238e7.summary: The council added a funding plan for the Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to its legislative priorities list.
607b9c8ee0b238e7.impact: This tells state lawmakers what Eagle Mountain wants money for; it does not build anything or commit city dollars. If the funding ever arrives, drivers on the Airport Road corridor would be the ones to notice.

60f7e94413bd6b60.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items moved
60f7e94413bd6b60.summary: The council approved its consent agenda and pulled the downtown plan and inland port resolutions out for separate debate later in the meeting.
60f7e94413bd6b60.impact: This one rearranged the evening's running order. Both pulled items got their own discussion; no resident is touched by the shuffle itself.

610608cbb6ff22dc.headline: Parking rule changes rejected
610608cbb6ff22dc.summary: The council moved to reject proposed changes to the city's parking rules.
610608cbb6ff22dc.impact: The parking rules stay exactly as they are today. There is nothing new you need to do, and no new restrictions on where you park.

6122b537a87857d2.headline: Jason Allen seated on the Planning Commission
6122b537a87857d2.summary: The council agreed to Jason Allen serving a three-year Planning Commission term, January 2026 through December 2028.
6122b537a87857d2.impact: Residents who show up to speak on a development proposal will find him among the commissioners hearing it. No other effect.

618b542767654bae.headline: Site plan approved for LKL Associates
618b542767654bae.summary: The council signed off on the site plan for LKL Associates, letting the project proceed on the layout submitted.
618b542767654bae.impact: Neighbors of the site are the people this touches. The motion names no address, no acreage and no use, so what will be built there is not in the record.

62e0b763f54dc1c3.headline: New affordable housing fund created
62e0b763f54dc1c3.summary: Eagle Mountain set up a separate city account, the Affordable Housing Fund, to hold and track money for affordable housing.
62e0b763f54dc1c3.impact: The account is a container: the motion does not put any dollars in it or name a project. Watch for later votes that decide what goes in and what it pays for.

639bc4a985b55efa.headline: Consent items changed: trees, $40,000 for parks
639bc4a985b55efa.summary: Approval of the consent agenda came with conditions: trees or their cash value from Stadion LLC, a $40,000 park donation from Comcast, and a revised meeting calendar.
639bc4a985b55efa.impact: The tree and park money comes out of development deals, not your utility bill, so nothing changes at home. If you attend meetings, the March 5 date is gone and March 6 and November 6 were added.

63a3c2704651aad5.headline: Budget reworked to match the certified rate
63a3c2704651aad5.summary: A second version of the 2026-27 budget came up, adjusted to reflect the newly certified property tax rate, with the city attorney asking for the motion to be clarified.
63a3c2704651aad5.impact: No outcome is recorded for this version of the motion. The spending plan itself was settled elsewhere in the same meeting.

64d01d1c7d363b27.headline: Rose Ranch farmland-to-housing rezone
