64d01d1c7d363b27.summary: The council weighed rezoning Rose Ranch from agriculture to the R2 and R3 housing zones, conditioned on crosswalks, a historical marker and finishing the Pony Express Trail.
64d01d1c7d363b27.impact: If it goes ahead, farmland at Rose Ranch becomes housing. Neighbors would get raised tabletop crosswalks and a historical marker on the Pony Express Trail, and the trail finished as usable space.

652689e1ffe0a542.headline: Lot line changes allowed by survey, not a plat
652689e1ffe0a542.summary: The council changed city code so a property line between a subdivision and an outlying parcel can be adjusted by survey instead of a plat amendment.
652689e1ffe0a542.impact: Shifting a boundary with a neighboring parcel now takes a survey rather than a full plat amendment. Staff will also record a zoning notice on the property, so future buyers can see when land sits in more than one zone.

65282e306887a4aa.headline: Site plan rules changed, siding swaps left out
65282e306887a4aa.summary: The council amended the city's site plan chapter but struck the proposed clause letting builders swap one approved exterior material for another.
65282e306887a4aa.impact: Builders and their architects deal with this when filing plans; swapping siding materials still needs the usual review. Homeowners will not notice.

662b66a778b2744e.headline: City budget amended to $156 million
662b66a778b2744e.summary: The council amended this year's city budget for the third time, setting the total at $155,990,118.
662b66a778b2744e.impact: This sets the ceiling on what the city can spend this budget year. The motion doesn't say what the money is for, so you won't see a specific change from this vote alone.

66f968a18f760bd1.headline: City buys 21 acres for a future civic campus
66f968a18f760bd1.summary: The city agreed to buy 20.99 acres of land from Ivory Homes and SITLA for a future civic campus.
66f968a18f760bd1.impact: The city now has land set aside for future civic buildings. Nothing is built yet: the motion doesn't say what will go there, what it cost, or when.

6777498a8c4a84b0.headline: Move to reject the fence rules got no second
6777498a8c4a84b0.summary: A motion to turn down the fencing code changes outright failed when no other councilmember seconded it.
6777498a8c4a84b0.impact: The rejection never came to a vote, so nothing was settled here. The fencing question moved forward under a different motion the same night.

6820f051bcd1f4fd.headline: Brett Wright named mayor pro tem for 2025
6820f051bcd1f4fd.summary: Councilmember Brett Wright was chosen as mayor pro tempore for 2025.
6820f051bcd1f4fd.impact: Wright runs council meetings when the mayor cannot attend. It decides who holds the gavel on a given night and nothing more.

69540fc766428341.headline: New city website, $35,000 contract
69540fc766428341.summary: The city hired Web Development Group Platforms to build a new city website for $35,000, leaving staff to settle a payment schedule.
69540fc766428341.impact: Anyone who uses the city site to find an agenda, a form or a meeting date will eventually land on a rebuilt version. No launch date was set.

698027249424544a.headline: Plat review deadline tied to state law
698027249424544a.summary: The council changed the subdivision approval section of city code so review timelines point to state code Chapter 10-9a rather than being spelled out separately.
698027249424544a.impact: Wording cleanup inside the development code. Builders filing preliminary plats deal with it; nobody else will notice.

6a82f26c55489d7a.headline: Council rejects change to home building rules
6a82f26c55489d7a.summary: The council turned down an ordinance that would have rewritten the city's zoning definitions and its residential development standards.
6a82f26c55489d7a.impact: The rules for building homes in Eagle Mountain stay as they are. Builders and anyone drawing up plans for a lot keep working from the existing standards.

6acdb3566ea57bbe.headline: Holbrook land use map change also shelved
6acdb3566ea57bbe.summary: A companion change to the city's future land use map for Cedar Valley Holbrook was set aside alongside the zoning request.
6acdb3566ea57bbe.impact: The Holbrook proposal stays frozen in place, map and zoning together. No deadline was set for bringing either back.

6b2b79b9c30c7af2.headline: Consent agenda approved
6b2b79b9c30c7af2.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote, with a change to one item that had been discussed earlier in the work session.
6b2b79b9c30c7af2.impact: This is routine housekeeping: the consent agenda is where the council batches items it does not need to debate one by one.

6bf94fddada9f71d.headline: One lot rezoned in Meadow Ranch
6bf94fddada9f71d.summary: The council approved a zoning change for a single property, Lot 433 in Meadow Ranch Plat 4.
6bf94fddada9f71d.impact: This affects one lot and its immediate neighbors, not the wider city. The motion does not say what the new zoning allows, so check with the city if you live nearby.

6c01b4fe054e32f4.headline: McDonald's site plan held for a traffic study
6c01b4fe054e32f4.summary: The council put off approving the McDonald's site plan in City Center until a traffic study is finished.
6c01b4fe054e32f4.impact: The restaurant cannot move ahead until traffic near City Center is studied. If you drive through that area, the study is meant to answer what a drive-through would do to it.

6c26283e0e57f64f.headline: Consent items approved, two pulled out
6c26283e0e57f64f.summary: The council approved a consent agenda of bond releases, minutes and site plans, pulling one item out for separate discussion and sending a school site plan back over an easement.
6c26283e0e57f64f.impact: Bundled housekeeping: warranty releases on finished subdivisions, past meeting minutes, and site plans staff already reviewed. The Alpine School District middle school plan returns later so the council can discuss vacating an easement.

6c40b5fe304a33f5.headline: Rules updated for accessory recreation buildings
6c40b5fe304a33f5.summary: The council changed the code section governing accessory recreation buildings; the motion itself does not spell out what the new rules say.
6c40b5fe304a33f5.impact: Planning a structure like this on your lot? Read the amended section before you file, because the record of this vote does not state what changed.

6cb716530b38110c.headline: Lennar put on notice over Ault Farms agreement
6cb716530b38110c.summary: The city formally notified Lennar Homes that it is in default on specific terms of the Ault Farms master development agreement.
6cb716530b38110c.impact: If you live in or near Ault Farms, this is the city pressing the builder to meet commitments it agreed to. The motion doesn't say which terms were missed or what happens next.

6d42d7a9159be015.headline: New rules to shift development rights between sites
6d42d7a9159be015.summary: The city created a transfer of development rights overlay zone, a tool that lets building density be moved from one property to another.
6d42d7a9159be015.impact: This mostly matters to landowners and developers: it opens a path to shift allowed homes off one parcel and onto another, which means density can land in different places than the base zoning suggests.

6e456e4d7c5e00b5.headline: Consent agenda approved, with trails added
6e456e4d7c5e00b5.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, adding "trails" to the scope of review in one of the items it covered.
6e456e4d7c5e00b5.impact: This is routine housekeeping: the consent agenda bundles uncontested items into one vote, and nothing here changes for residents.

6eb156bed489b878.headline: Transportation Master Plan adopted
6eb156bed489b878.summary: The council adopted the city's Transportation Master Plan, the blueprint for which roads get built and widened as Eagle Mountain grows.
6eb156bed489b878.impact: The plan itself does not break ground or spend money, but it decides which routes the city plans around. If a future road runs near your street, this document is where it first appears.

6f0bff804a840759.headline: Harmony 13 subdivision plan denied
6f0bff804a840759.summary: The council rejected the preliminary plat, the proposed lot layout, for the Harmony 13 subdivision.
6f0bff804a840759.impact: As drawn, Harmony 13 does not move forward. That touches the developer and neighbors near the site; the motion itself gives no reasons for the denial.

6f2ce38fdefe909d.headline: City fee schedule updated
6f2ce38fdefe909d.summary: The council approved changes to Appendix A of the city's consolidated fee schedule, the price list for city services and permits.
6f2ce38fdefe909d.impact: Some of what you pay the city changes. The motion does not say which fees or by how much, so check the current schedule before pulling a permit or paying for a city service.

6f8197042b5d4524.headline: Two items pulled off the consent list
6f8197042b5d4524.summary: The council passed its consent agenda after pulling items 13.A. and 13.C. out for open discussion.
6f8197042b5d4524.impact: The effect was to give two items a real airing instead of a bundled vote. Nothing lands on residents here.

7057ff3826d426d1.headline: Hidden Hollow keeps its pool
7057ff3826d426d1.summary: The council rejected Cadence Homes' request to swap the planned swimming pool at the Hidden Hollow clubhouse for a gym and lawn games.
7057ff3826d426d1.impact: If you live in or are buying into Hidden Hollow, the clubhouse amenity stays as it was originally approved: a swimming pool, not a gym.

705a43342717c003.headline: December named PTA centennial month
705a43342717c003.summary: The council proclaimed December 2025 as Utah PTA Centennial Celebration Month, marking 100 years of the parent teacher association in the state.
705a43342717c003.impact: A ceremonial nod to the PTA's anniversary. It carries no money and no rules.

724181ab2d215bdd.headline: Youth Council vote retaken to include mayor
724181ab2d215bdd.summary: After the city attorney noted Mayor Westmoreland had been left out of the required vote, the council reopened the Youth Council code rewrite.
724181ab2d215bdd.impact: A procedural fix to a vote taken minutes earlier. It touches the record only.

72c2bf4a2d8fdc5c.headline: Rezoning of two parcels for houses denied
72c2bf4a2d8fdc5c.summary: The council rejected a request to rezone one parcel and part of another from village core commercial and community open space to the RC residential zone.
72c2bf4a2d8fdc5c.impact: That ground keeps its commercial and open space zoning, so the 59 houses the applicant proposed will not go ahead under this application. Nothing changes on the land itself.

72c99c3d5fc55f98.headline: City to draft telecom rules
72c99c3d5fc55f98.summary: The council added a telecommunications ordinance, a franchise agreement, or both to its list of legislative priorities for staff to work on.
72c99c3d5fc55f98.impact: No rule exists yet, so nothing changes for phone or internet customers. Whatever staff draft would have to come back to the council before it means anything.

72fde0ed6104cf51.headline: Vote on item 16.A property chart
72fde0ed6104cf51.summary: Item 16.A came to a vote on the terms of a chart of affected properties; the record does not show what the item covers or how it ended.
72fde0ed6104cf51.impact: Without a description or a result in the record, there is nothing here we can tell you about your own property. The chart in the meeting packet is the place to check.

734dfd285cc9605e.headline: New recreation, arts, and parks tax created
734dfd285cc9605e.summary: The city wrote a new Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax into its municipal code, adding a chapter that establishes the tax.
734dfd285cc9605e.impact: This puts the tax on the books. The motion itself doesn't state a rate or a start date, so check the ordinance for what you would actually pay and when.

742f29587bd6c256.headline: Angeline Washburn joins Youth Council advisers
742f29587bd6c256.summary: The council appointed Angeline Washburn as a Youth Council advisory for a one-year term through June 2025.
742f29587bd6c256.impact: The agenda listed a city office lease amendment under this item, so the written record does not match the motion as recorded. The appointment itself reaches only the Youth Council program.

747ebedc1ff0caed.headline: Consent agenda passed, two items pulled
747ebedc1ff0caed.summary: The council pulled two items off its consent agenda for separate discussion and approved everything else in a single vote.
747ebedc1ff0caed.impact: Housekeeping items cleared together, with two held back for their own hearing. Nothing lands on a resident at this step.

768e3c2ad0e8b9ef.headline: Consent agenda approved
768e3c2ad0e8b9ef.summary: The council cleared its consent agenda, the batch of routine items handled in one vote; the record does not list what was in it.
768e3c2ad0e8b9ef.impact: Consent items are the ones nobody flagged for discussion. Nothing here lands on your street or your bill.

77b630b74967d885.headline: Emily Hoehne joins Library Advisory Board
77b630b74967d885.summary: Emily Hoehne was appointed to the Library Advisory Board, serving from the date of the vote through December 31, 2025.
77b630b74967d885.impact: One volunteer seat gets filled at the library board. Library hours, services, and cards stay exactly as they are.

79609f4529811ca5.headline: New standards for RV and trailer storage
79609f4529811ca5.summary: The council rewrote the city's rules for outdoor storage of recreational vehicles and trailers, changing the standards that apply to that use.
79609f4529811ca5.impact: This touches properties used to store RVs and trailers outdoors: storage yard owners and operators more than ordinary homeowners. The record doesn't spell out the new requirements, so check the updated chapter before relying on the old rules.

7a165bf8fcb02408.headline: Overland development deal amended, lights capped at 25 feet
7a165bf8fcb02408.summary: The city approved a change to the Overland development agreement, requiring 25-foot light poles instead of 30-foot and a finished 35-acre land swap with the state.
7a165bf8fcb02408.impact: If you live near the Overland project, outdoor lighting will sit five feet lower than planned, which means less glare. The deal also depends on a state land exchange tied to the planned bypass road.

7bba93771e07f46e.headline: Energy rules for new buildings put on hold
7bba93771e07f46e.summary: The council set aside proposed changes to the city's energy-related building rules without deciding them.
7bba93771e07f46e.impact: The current rules still apply, so builders and homeowners plan under the standards already on the books until the council picks the item back up.

7bbbf065a021484c.headline: Site plan approved for Firefly plats 4 and 5
7bbbf065a021484c.summary: The city approved the site plan for Firefly NPA 1A, plats 4 and 5, in the southwest part of the city near Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway and Pole Canyon Boulevard.
7bbbf065a021484c.impact: If you live in the southwest end of the city, expect building on this parcel to move ahead. The motion does not say how many homes or lots are involved.

7bf90f6f13018de0.headline: Cemetery board appointment
7bf90f6f13018de0.summary: Marian Burningham was appointed to the Cemetery Advisory Board for a three year term running through December 31, 2027.
7bf90f6f13018de0.impact: One volunteer seat filled on a board that advises on the city cemetery. No effect on daily life here.

7c86c8b984ecdcee.headline: Change order on the sewer plant upgrade
7c86c8b984ecdcee.summary: The council approved a change order with engineering firm Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services for the wastewater treatment plant upgrade.
7c86c8b984ecdcee.impact: This adjusts the engineering contract on the city's sewer plant upgrade. You will not see anything different at home; the plant work continues under revised terms.

7ca89e1d86abe0a3.headline: Changes to the Ault Farms (Parkway Fields) development deal
7ca89e1d86abe0a3.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the Ault Farms (Parkway Fields) master development agreement, adding a nine-month sunset clause to the amendment.
7ca89e1d86abe0a3.impact: This touches the Parkway Fields area rather than the city at large, and the amended terms expire after nine months. The motion itself does not say what else in the agreement changed.

7d6eda8f4284ed04.headline: Revised plan for Town Center marketplace
7d6eda8f4284ed04.summary: The council approved an amended preliminary plat for the Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center.
7d6eda8f4284ed04.impact: This is an early planning step for the Town Center marketplace, laying out how the land is divided. Nothing gets built on this approval alone.

7e051171013c9991.headline: Consent agenda approved in one vote
7e051171013c9991.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items handled together without separate discussion.
7e051171013c9991.impact: The record here does not list what was in the batch, so there is nothing specific to point you to. Consent items are the ones the council did not consider worth debating.

7ebb1a9627558b14.headline: City backs an inland port area in Eagle Mountain
7ebb1a9627558b14.summary: The council voted to support creating a Utah Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain, endorsing state involvement in local development.
7ebb1a9627558b14.impact: An inland port area lets a state authority direct development and tax money within its boundaries. The motion does not name the location or acreage, so watch for the boundary to be set later.

7f0c6df5efdcea0a.headline: ShaRee Curtis gets a two-year board term
7f0c6df5efdcea0a.summary: The council appointed ShaRee Curtis to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2028.
7f0c6df5efdcea0a.impact: Volunteer seat, two years, no cost or change to residents.

7fa70e7d9e820261.headline: Nathan Washburn joins Youth Council advisers
7fa70e7d9e820261.summary: The council appointed Nathan Washburn as a Youth Council advisory for a one-year term through June 2025.
7fa70e7d9e820261.impact: Teenagers in the Youth Council program and their parents will meet this adviser. For everyone else in the city, the appointment passes unnoticed.

8023ac051bf7cc07.headline: Fence and retaining wall rules held back
8023ac051bf7cc07.summary: The council set aside a rewrite of the city's rules on privacy fences, landscaping buffers and retaining walls without setting a return date.
8023ac051bf7cc07.impact: If you were planning a fence or a retaining wall, the current rules still stand. No new date was set for a decision.

806ae8c9a1412570.headline: Block grant money set: $150K for small businesses
806ae8c9a1412570.summary: The city set its 2026 federal block grant spending: $150,000 in small business grants, $36,163 for yard cleanup, $20,000 for an ADA crosswalk, and $35,292 in aid programs.
806ae8c9a1412570.impact: Small businesses can apply for grant money, and lower-income households get help with utility bills, cemetery costs, school supplies, food and yard cleanup. A new ADA ramp and crosswalk is funded at Fiona Street and Airport Road.

806e6799f0ba53b4.headline: Jacob Adams joins the Youth Council
806e6799f0ba53b4.summary: Jacob Adams was appointed to the Youth Council for a term ending June 30, 2025.
806e6799f0ba53b4.impact: One seat on a youth advisory body gets filled. This one touches the young person taking it and nobody else.

807b264076c36dee.headline: Marian Burningham joins Community Services Board
807b264076c36dee.summary: The council appointed Marian Burningham to the Community Services Board for a three-year term running to March 2029.
807b264076c36dee.impact: The board advises the city on parks and recreation programs. Filling a seat on it is not something you will notice day to day.

80cc314a6931926d.headline: Berry property rezoned for foothill homes
80cc314a6931926d.summary: The city rezoned the land known as the Berry property from agriculture to foothill residential, opening it to housing.
80cc314a6931926d.impact: The land can now be developed as foothill housing instead of staying farmland. Neighbors should expect a housing project to move forward there, though the motion sets no timeline or number of homes.

80e8c83b7c065688.headline: City hall design moved up the lobbying list
80e8c83b7c065688.summary: The council marked city hall land purchase and mortgage assistance as done, and made designing a new city hall a top legislative priority.
80e8c83b7c065688.impact: This sets what the city asks state lawmakers for. Nothing changes on the ground yet, and no building has been approved.

81ba05b85bb5aab4.headline: City Center commercial lot split approved
81ba05b85bb5aab4.summary: The council signed off on amending the recorded plat for Lot 1 of City Center Commercial Phase A, letting the owners carve out another commercial lot.
81ba05b85bb5aab4.impact: Owners of the site can now divide it and build on or sell the new piece. Homes backing onto the property get the partial screening wall finished once the site is developed.

82662ff9bde0930c.headline: Open space plan adopted, backyard trail dropped
82662ff9bde0930c.summary: The council adopted the city's natural open space and wildlife habitat plan, but cut a walking path planned behind homes between Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane.
82662ff9bde0930c.impact: Homeowners along Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane will not get a path behind their backyards, though the land stays classified as open space. The plan also drops its semi-truck parking language and lets goat grazing run as needed rather than on a fixed schedule.

8296592ec7cf7407.headline: Up to 20.35 acres near Bypass Road to be traded
8296592ec7cf7407.summary: The council approved disposing of up to 20.35 acres of city-owned land known as the Bypass Road Property, to be exchanged for land chosen later.
8296592ec7cf7407.impact: The city is clearing the way to swap this land, but has not yet said what it will get in return. Staff must come back to the council before any trade is final.

832f461559fb6318.headline: 10% of new homes in some zones must be affordable
832f461559fb6318.summary: The city now requires at least 10% of new homes in certain residential zones to be priced for households earning 80% or less of Utah County's median income.
832f461559fb6318.impact: If you build or buy in these zones, a share of the homes carry a recorded deed restriction: the owner must live there and the price is capped. Applies to new development, not existing homes.

83f4f90245751c88.headline: KJ Call named youth council mayor
83f4f90245751c88.summary: KJ Call will lead the Youth City Council as its mayor until the next Youth Council election, under an appointment the council approved.
83f4f90245751c88.impact: A title for one student, and a line for the city's youth program. Nothing in how the city runs shifts.

843d1280437f391d.headline: Parks plan adopted, Sweetwater Park added
843d1280437f391d.summary: The city adopted its parks, trails and open space master plan along with the impact fee plan that pays for it, adding Sweetwater Park's cost to the list.
843d1280437f391d.impact: This is the city's list of parks and trails it intends to build, and the fees charged on new construction that fund them. Sweetwater Park is now part of that funded list.

84ddbf698a381613.headline: Public art rules changed
84ddbf698a381613.summary: The council approved changes to the city's public art rules in Chapter 12.35 of the municipal code.
84ddbf698a381613.impact: The record doesn't say what changed. The chapter governs how the city handles public art, so there's no stated change to what you pay or do.

857d6838d22c07be.headline: City to gather housing data, plan west-side roads
857d6838d22c07be.summary: The council added two items to its state legislative priorities: collecting data on existing housing types and sizes, and planning new transportation corridors for the city's south and west ends.
857d6838d22c07be.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. This sets what city staff research and what they raise with state lawmakers, and it puts a future road west of Mid Valley on the planning map.

85e5eb66751b27f8.headline: Street naming rules for new subdivisions
85e5eb66751b27f8.summary: The council amended the preliminary plat section of city code to deal with how streets in new subdivisions get named.
85e5eb66751b27f8.impact: Whoever names the roads in the next subdivision works under different language now. Your existing address is unaffected.

86c9c93aa846efb7.headline: Ask the state about archery at Rodeo Grounds
86c9c93aa846efb7.summary: The council put archery shooting at the Rodeo Grounds on its list of priorities to raise with state lawmakers.
86c9c93aa846efb7.impact: No archery range exists or is funded by this. It flags the idea for the city's state lobbying and nothing more.

86d5a3525b0cf554.headline: Rec center funding pulled, $1M pooled for parks
86d5a3525b0cf554.summary: The council reworked how proceeds from the utility sale are spent, moving $2.6 million earmarked for a recreation center into unallocated funds and pooling $1 million for parks.
86d5a3525b0cf554.impact: A recreation center is off the funding list for now: council members said it could be revisited later, possibly starting with buying land. The $1 million park fund still covers Silver Lake amphitheater, bike park, and Nolan Park improvements.

884b312d354f5469.headline: Hillside building rules held back
884b312d354f5469.summary: The council delayed a set of changes to the city's slope development rules, which govern building on steep ground.
884b312d354f5469.impact: Builders working hillside lots keep planning under the rules already on the books. If you are not developing on a slope, this one passes you by.

8911703b3b2ae71b.headline: Development deal set for Spring Run Plaza
8911703b3b2ae71b.summary: The council approved the master development agreement for Spring Run Plaza, capping the required landscaping width at 10 feet and allowing engineered retaining walls taller than 6 feet without tiering.
8911703b3b2ae71b.impact: This sets the rules the developer must build to at that corner. You may see tall, untiered retaining walls there, though stacked boulder and rock walls are not allowed.

89860402b8caa537.headline: New rules for building on steep slopes
89860402b8caa537.summary: The city rewrote four sections of its code governing development on steep slopes, changing how hillside land may be built on.
89860402b8caa537.impact: If you own hillside land or plan to build on a slope, the rules for what you can put there have changed. Residents on flatter ground are unaffected.

8a6b740387bed2d3.headline: Market study hired for Eagle's Landing
8a6b740387bed2d3.summary: The council hired Economic & Planning Systems to study demand for Eagle's Landing, a large commercial project on Pony Express Parkway north of downtown.
8a6b740387bed2d3.impact: The study takes one to three months and feeds a decision on whether to use a TIF bond for roads and utilities there. Nothing breaks ground yet.

8aaadeedeeeb1a16.headline: Three consent items approved separately
8aaadeedeeeb1a16.summary: The council approved the three items it had pulled out of the consent agenda, Items 10.A., 10.B. and 12.A., in a single vote.
8aaadeedeeeb1a16.impact: The record does not say what these three items contain, so nothing here tells you what changed. One member sat out the vote.

8aea3cf68abd26db.headline: Zayo fiber franchise agreement put on hold
8aea3cf68abd26db.summary: The council set aside a decision on a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, the telecom company, rather than voting it up or down.
8aea3cf68abd26db.impact: Nothing changes for now. The agreement would govern Zayo's use of city rights of way for fiber, and it can come back to a future meeting.

8b163ac877929e92.headline: Federal housing grant plan sent to Washington
8b163ac877929e92.summary: The council signed off on Eagle Mountain's spending plan for its 2026 federal Community Development Block Grant money and sent it to HUD for approval.
8b163ac877929e92.impact: HUD requires this plan before the city can draw its block grant funds. The motion names no projects or amounts, so nothing here tells you what the money will buy.

8ca676754311bed6.headline: Residential zoning rules queued for review
8ca676754311bed6.summary: The council queued Chapter 17.25, the city's residential zoning rules, for a future review, without changing anything in the rules themselves.
8ca676754311bed6.impact: Nothing about what you can build on your lot changes today. If the review produces edits, they would come back to the council before taking effect.

8d133968ed8a08d2.headline: Public comment moved later in the meeting
8d133968ed8a08d2.summary: The council moved the public comment period to a later point in the meeting.
8d133968ed8a08d2.impact: Residents who came to speak did so later in the evening. Nothing else changes.

8e0703e7da922819.headline: New rules for hiring a city manager
8e0703e7da922819.summary: The city rewrote the code covering its top appointed job, renaming it city manager and setting how a vacancy is filled and candidates recruited.
8e0703e7da922819.impact: Candidate interviews stay closed to the public, so when the job next opens you will see the appointment rather than the choosing. Nothing about city services changes.

8e740e62aee93d38.headline: Earlier draft of the front yard parking rule
8e740e62aee93d38.summary: The council took up an earlier version of the front yard parking change, striking one section and adding trailers and other vehicles; no outcome is recorded.
8e740e62aee93d38.impact: This wording never reached your street. The version that governs front yard parking is the one the council settled on later the same night.

8e812934d688ef7c.headline: Hire a lobbyist for $60,000 a year
8e812934d688ef7c.summary: The city hired an outside lobbying firm to represent Eagle Mountain for one year at $60,000.
8e812934d688ef7c.impact: The money comes out of the city budget to press Eagle Mountain's case at the Legislature. Nothing changes at your door or on your bill.

8eda2d3a3da35661.headline: Mortgage help: city loans up to $25,000
8eda2d3a3da35661.summary: The city created a mortgage assistance program offering homebuyers loans of up to $25,000, prioritized by job type and then by lower household income.
8eda2d3a3da35661.impact: If you're buying a home in Eagle Mountain, you can apply for up to $25,000 toward the purchase. Households of six or more earning up to $151,800 may qualify, and an outside reviewer will check eligibility.

8efb0379a58bd336.headline: New historic zone created in city code
8efb0379a58bd336.summary: The council added a new "historic" zoning category to city code, striking one section (17.32.010(D)) from the version that was proposed.
8efb0379a58bd336.impact: No land was rezoned by this vote. But if your property is later placed in a historic zone, you would face extra rules on what you can build or change.

8f1c0ba0411f180f.headline: City code definitions amended
8f1c0ba0411f180f.summary: The council amended the definitions section of the city code, Section 17.10.030; the motion does not say which definitions changed.
8f1c0ba0411f180f.impact: The motion gives no detail on what was redefined, so there is nothing here that clearly changes anything for residents.

8f2ea24055e3e673.headline: Board appointment terms shift to an April start
8f2ea24055e3e673.summary: The city changed its code so library board and other appointments run April 1 through March 31 instead of the calendar year.
8f2ea24055e3e673.impact: This touches people who serve on city boards, not the public. If you sit on one, your term now starts in April rather than January.

8f8a3cb4ba0a391e.headline: Building and construction standards updated
8f8a3cb4ba0a391e.summary: The council adopted an updated Title 15, the city's building and construction standards, which now carries truck route approval requirements.
8f8a3cb4ba0a391e.impact: Contractors and engineers filing plans build to the new standards from here. For everyone else this is a technical manual you will never open.

8f94fc7f68d413d2.headline: Residential development standards amended
8f94fc7f68d413d2.summary: The council amended its residential development standards, section 17.25.040, though the minutes do not record what the amendment changed.
8f94fc7f68d413d2.impact: Rules for what goes into new subdivisions moved here, but the record is too thin to say how it lands on any particular street.

903efc4f2a54085b.headline: Impact fee cut for new businesses
903efc4f2a54085b.summary: The city partially suspended its transportation impact fee for nonresidential development, and dropped the carve-out that had applied to restaurants at every building size.
903efc4f2a54085b.impact: If you are building a business, store, or office in Eagle Mountain, you will pay less in road impact fees. The restaurant carve-out no longer applies at any size.

908e85a88dacf65d.headline: Arbor Day set for April 25
908e85a88dacf65d.summary: The council proclaimed April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day in Eagle Mountain.
908e85a88dacf65d.impact: Ceremonial only, the kind of item that keeps the city's tree program recognized. It asks nothing of residents.

90a1c2083f51a27d.headline: New advisory board for older residents
90a1c2083f51a27d.summary: The council created a Senior Citizens Advisory Board in city code, giving older residents a standing group to advise the city.
90a1c2083f51a27d.impact: If you are a senior in Eagle Mountain, there is now a formal channel to raise concerns to the council. The board advises; it does not decide.

90d437975599839c.headline: Big Eagle 7 land rezoned for industrial use
90d437975599839c.summary: The council rezoned the land known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial zoning and applied an RTI overlay zone on top of it.
90d437975599839c.impact: This land is now set aside for industrial use rather than homes. If you live near Big Eagle 7, what gets built there in the future will be industrial.

90f4eb56507a2198.headline: Vote to deny the Harmony 14 subdivision plan
90f4eb56507a2198.summary: The council considered rejecting the preliminary plat, the proposed lot layout, for the Harmony 14 subdivision.
90f4eb56507a2198.impact: This is the step where the city signs off on how a subdivision is laid out, so it affects the Harmony 14 developer and anyone living near the site. The record here gives no reasons.

913e8b0a8982e106.headline: Redraw lot lines at Steeplechase South
913e8b0a8982e106.summary: The council approved a second plat amendment for the Steeplechase South subdivision at 877 N Pony Express Parkway, adjusting the recorded subdivision map.
913e8b0a8982e106.impact: This touches property boundaries inside one subdivision on Pony Express Parkway. If you do not own or plan to build on land there, it passes you by.

9199d4b0d3ed38e1.headline: Future land use map redrawn for master plan area
9199d4b0d3ed38e1.summary: The city redrew its long-range land use map for 27 parcels in the Eagle Mountain Properties area, designating large stretches as parks and open space, business park, and community commercial.
9199d4b0d3ed38e1.impact: This is the city's plan for what the land should eventually become, not a permit to build. It signals where future parks, shops, and business parks may go.

920a39d6593938ff.headline: Water master plan and impact fee study adopted
920a39d6593938ff.summary: The council adopted the city's long-range plan for drinking water, along with the impact fee facilities plan that goes with it.
920a39d6593938ff.impact: Builders pay attention here: the plan is the engineering basis the city uses to justify water impact fees on new construction. If you already have a house and a water meter, nothing about your service changes today.

933ecc894562afd9.headline: Chad Decoursey fills Planning Commission seat
933ecc894562afd9.summary: The council appointed Chad Decoursey to the Planning Commission to finish a vacated term, from May 2026 through March 2027.
933ecc894562afd9.impact: A seat that had been sitting empty now has someone in it through next March. This one touches the commission's roster and nobody else.

93e5fc05941a0f2f.headline: Six wayfinding signs from Impact Signs
93e5fc05941a0f2f.summary: The council took up an agreement with Impact Signs to supply six wayfinding signs; the motion doesn't state a cost.
93e5fc05941a0f2f.impact: If it moves ahead, you'd see six new directional signs around the city. Nothing else changes.

94d77853e78b1388.headline: November named Hunger Awareness Month
94d77853e78b1388.summary: The council declared November 2025 Hunger Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
94d77853e78b1388.impact: A proclamation carries no rule and no money behind it. The council put the city's name to the cause for the month, and nothing you pay or do changes.

95230ee814ac6a81.headline: Mid-Valley deal signed with Terra Smith's
95230ee814ac6a81.summary: Council members signed off on a participation agreement between the city, its redevelopment agency and Terra Smith's Eagle Mountain LLC for the Mid-Valley project area.
95230ee814ac6a81.impact: A private developer is now tied into the Mid-Valley project area. The terms are not laid out in the motion, so what gets built there is not settled by this line alone.

9592a88121c12468.headline: Walden Park Road money moved to Mid Valley Road
9592a88121c12468.summary: The council amended its 2023-24 budget to take Capital Fund money set aside for Walden Park Road and put it toward widening Mid Valley Road.
9592a88121c12468.impact: Drivers on Mid Valley Road are the ones who stand to gain. Walden Park Road loses the money it was holding this budget year, with no replacement named in the motion.

96884106578745e6.headline: Consent agenda approved with one item pulled
96884106578745e6.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, pulling one for separate discussion and folding in corrections to the March 18 minutes.
96884106578745e6.impact: Housekeeping that clears the small stuff in a single vote. You will not notice any of it.

97d87823c9cde42c.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
97d87823c9cde42c.summary: The council passed its consent agenda after moving item 13.A. to scheduled items for more discussion and dropping item 14.C. from the agenda.
97d87823c9cde42c.impact: Housekeeping for how the night's business was handled. Item 13.A. got its own debate later in the meeting and 14.C. was not decided at all.

986d5d7fead215c5.headline: Storm water rules updated
986d5d7fead215c5.summary: The council amended the city's storm water ordinance, the rules covering runoff and drainage.
986d5d7fead215c5.impact: The motion doesn't say what changed, so it points to no specific effect on residents. Rules like these mainly govern builders and how new development handles runoff.

988a3cbedcd369fc.headline: Chad Decoursey joins planning commission as alternate
988a3cbedcd369fc.summary: Chad Decoursey was appointed a Planning Commission alternate for a three-year term running through December 2028.
988a3cbedcd369fc.impact: An alternate fills in when a regular commissioner is absent. If you bring a development or zoning item to the commission, he may be one of the people hearing it.

98ab14e03fe7ad4a.headline: Two consent items pulled for discussion
98ab14e03fe7ad4a.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled items 11.A and 14.B out for separate debate and dropped item 14.D from the agenda.
98ab14e03fe7ad4a.impact: A procedural sorting of the night's business. What the pulled items contain is decided later, not here.

9a1c4f90aa3672d6.headline: Earlier tax increase repealed
9a1c4f90aa3672d6.summary: Eagle Mountain repealed the property tax increase above the certified rate that it had adopted for 2026-27, clearing the way for a replacement rate set the same night.
9a1c4f90aa3672d6.impact: This wipes the earlier increase off the books. Read it alongside the rate the council adopted afterward, which is the one that reaches your bill.

9a23406c979c5088.headline: Adam Jacobs joins the library board
9a23406c979c5088.summary: Adam Jacobs was appointed to the Library Advisory Board for three years, through 2027.
9a23406c979c5088.impact: A second seat on the same volunteer board was filled the same night. Library hours, services and fees are untouched.

9a73c651d5e27bfb.headline: Firefly NPA 9.A site plan approved
9a73c651d5e27bfb.summary: The council approved the master site plan for Firefly NPA 9.A, the layout that governs how that part of the Firefly area gets built.
9a73c651d5e27bfb.impact: This clears the way for building in that section of Firefly. The motion does not state what is going in or how much, so the details sit in the site plan itself.

9a7ea80a7ff998ff.headline: Property tax raised to collect $5.6M more
9a7ea80a7ff998ff.summary: The council set the city property tax rate at 0.001500 for the coming year, nearly triple the certified rate of 0.000530, raising about $5.6 million in added revenue.
9a7ea80a7ff998ff.impact: Every property owner in Eagle Mountain pays more, with the city's share of the bill up 183% before new growth. The school and county lines on your tax notice are set by others and are untouched.

9ac9c33945e1ee9d.headline: Consent agenda approved in one vote
9ac9c33945e1ee9d.summary: The council passed its consent agenda, the batch of items handled together without separate discussion.
9ac9c33945e1ee9d.impact: The record here does not list which items were in the batch, so nothing can be said about who they touch.

9bd684a3c75fc825.headline: Study speed bumps for city streets
9bd684a3c75fc825.summary: The council added a review of speed bumps and speed tables to its Legislative Priorities List, the running list of items the city wants to work on.
9bd684a3c75fc825.impact: Nothing has been built or funded here. It puts traffic calming on the list of things the city intends to look at, so any actual bumps on your street are still some way off.

9c30a77b7d1340bf.headline: Rose Ranch subdivision agreement approved
9c30a77b7d1340bf.summary: The city approved a master development agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision, striking one water rights sentence and directing staff to keep negotiating a water delivery schedule.
9c30a77b7d1340bf.impact: Rose Ranch can now move ahead under an agreed set of terms, so expect building in that area. The water piece isn't settled: staff will keep negotiating when and how the developer turns over water.

9c673da62350dec7.headline: Legislative to-do list updated
9c673da62350dec7.summary: The council marked a review of conditional uses in the zoning code complete and dropped a tabled item on lot sizes in Neighborhood Residential 1.
9c673da62350dec7.impact: Housekeeping on the council's own list of pending work. Nothing about the rules on your property changed here.

9cce80d294e470c0.headline: New park and city signs sent back to staff
9cce80d294e470c0.summary: The council rejected a contract with Identity Signs for six new wayfinding signs and told staff to find sturdier materials and cheaper installation.
9cce80d294e470c0.impact: The aging signs directing you to parks like Smith Ranch Park stay as they are for now, and new ones will not go up this fall as staff had hoped.

9d24930397b4852d.headline: Backing for the 250th anniversary committee
9d24930397b4852d.summary: The council endorsed America250 Utah and recognized a local committee to plan Eagle Mountain's part in the nation's 250th anniversary.
9d24930397b4852d.impact: A volunteer committee now has the city's blessing to organize commemorations. Watch for events, but this resolution itself spends nothing and asks nothing of you.

9d45f0489af82101.headline: New rules for closing roads during construction
9d45f0489af82101.summary: The city rewrote its road-closure rules, requiring contractors to submit a traffic control plan and a plan for notifying residents seven days before working in the street.
9d45f0489af82101.impact: If crews are about to tear up your street, they now need an approved plan for warning you first. Contractors must get a permit and give the city notice before any work starts.

9d9e3c20c4c640b0.headline: Bigger no-build buffer around natural washes
9d9e3c20c4c640b0.summary: The council took up a rule barring permanent buildings and earthwork within 75 feet of a wash's center flowline, or 50 feet from its bank, whichever is greater.
9d9e3c20c4c640b0.impact: If your lot backs onto a dry wash, this limits how close you can build or dig. It applies to homes, shops, and business parks alike, with the city engineer measuring the buffer.

9da027445fa014ee.headline: Enyo development agreement taken up
9da027445fa014ee.summary: The council considered an ordinance approving a development agreement with Enyo, as written in the meeting's agenda packet.
9da027445fa014ee.impact: A development agreement sets what a developer may build and what the city requires in return. The motion itself gives no location, size, or dollar figures, so the terms are only in the packet.

9da657a0a578c38f.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled
9da657a0a578c38f.summary: Grouped routine items passed together, with item 10.A held back for later.
9da657a0a578c38f.impact: Batch housekeeping, the kind the council clears in a single vote. Residents feel none of it.

9ea6ef667575e4a9.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
9ea6ef667575e4a9.summary: The council passed its batch of consent items after pulling items 12.A. and 13.A. out for separate discussion.
9ea6ef667575e4a9.impact: A bundling step that clears uncontested business in one vote. The two pulled items got their own airing; this motion itself reaches no resident.

9eb6b795dde6870c.headline: Change to the Eagle Quest East development deal
9eb6b795dde6870c.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the master development agreement covering the Eagle Quest East project.
9eb6b795dde6870c.impact: The motion does not spell out what changed. A master development agreement sets the ground rules for how a project area gets built, so this matters mainly to the developer and to people living near Eagle Quest East.

9ebff98d296b5fb7.headline: New school district with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield
9ebff98d296b5fb7.summary: The council took up an agreement with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield Town to create their own school district, and backed five neighboring cities forming a central district.
9ebff98d296b5fb7.impact: If you have school-age children, this points toward a district shared with Saratoga Springs and Fairfield rather than the one your schools sit in now. What changes in classrooms and on tax bills was not settled here.

a03274ba9d9098a6.headline: Marcia Vasquez appointed to library board
a03274ba9d9098a6.summary: Marcia Vasquez was appointed a Library Board advisor for a three-year term through December 2028.
a03274ba9d9098a6.impact: The board advises on how the library runs. Library hours, cards and services are unchanged by the appointment itself.

a1820ed606c35e63.headline: Four zoning code sections updated
a1820ed606c35e63.summary: The council amended four sections of the city's zoning code; the motion gives no detail on what the changes actually do.
a1820ed606c35e63.impact: We can't tell you what changed: the record names only section numbers. They sit in Title 17, the zoning rules that govern what can be built and where.

a1b98064873923a3.headline: Change the fee for site plan amendments
a1b98064873923a3.summary: The council amended the city fee schedule to change what it charges for site plan amendments; the motion does not state the new amount.
a1b98064873923a3.impact: This touches builders and businesses that want to change an already-approved site plan, not ordinary homeowners. The record does not say what the fee now costs.

a4a986704789d041.headline: Two foot setback floated for side yard parking
a4a986704789d041.summary: The council also weighed a version allowing parking on the driveway, garage side and side yard on hard surface, kept two feet back from the sidewalk.
a4a986704789d041.impact: A draft, not a rule: the record shows no result for this wording. Nothing here binds a homeowner.

a5a48ae00479ee2e.headline: Election results certified; RAP tax passes
a5a48ae00479ee2e.summary: The council certified the November 4 election, declaring Jared R. Gray mayor, Brett L. Wright and Craig Whiting councilmembers, and the RAP tax approved by voters.
a5a48ae00479ee2e.impact: Your new mayor and two councilmembers are now officially elected, and Proposition 8, the RAP tax, is formally adopted because voters approved it.

a63c4185b40e9de3.headline: Consent agenda approved with two changes
a63c4185b40e9de3.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after fixing a typo on one item to read 2026-2027 and pulling another item out for separate discussion.
a63c4185b40e9de3.impact: Bundled housekeeping items cleared in one vote. The date fix and the item moved to the main agenda are procedural steps only.

a63fb54cd106b0ee.headline: Agreement approved over the Overland area
a63fb54cd106b0ee.summary: The council approved a memorandum of agreement concerning Overland; the motion itself does not spell out the terms.
a63fb54cd106b0ee.impact: The record gives no detail on what the city agreed to, so no effect on residents can honestly be described. It was pulled off the consent agenda for separate discussion.

a7405730033f900c.headline: Road plan adds E 1000 N, drops Canyon Wash link
a7405730033f900c.summary: The council updated the city road plan, adding E 1000 N as a minor collector from Pony Express Parkway to the East Expressway and dropping a Canyon Wash connection.
a7405730033f900c.impact: If you live near E 1000 N, that stretch is now mapped as a through road between Pony Express Parkway and the East Expressway, and the Canyon Wash connection is off the map. Nothing is built yet; the plan also steers impact fees.

a7744473c3e867db.headline: Melissa Clark named Mayor Pro Tempore
a7744473c3e867db.summary: The council appointed Melissa Clark as Mayor Pro Tempore, the member who runs meetings when the mayor is absent.
a7744473c3e867db.impact: A standing-in arrangement for council meetings. Nothing about city services or your bills changes.

a8258678df50b0fb.headline: Harmony development agreement amended
a8258678df50b0fb.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the development agreement covering the Harmony preliminary plat.
a8258678df50b0fb.impact: This changes the terms the Harmony developer must build to. The motion doesn't say what was changed, so it gives you nothing concrete about what will look different on the ground.

a845f0fcca8f59ae.headline: Buy 21 acres for a future civic campus
a845f0fcca8f59ae.summary: The council agreed to buy 20.99 acres from Ivory Homes and SITLA for a future civic campus, dropping proposed limits on commercial building size.
a845f0fcca8f59ae.impact: The city now owns the ground where future public buildings will sit. Removing the size cap leaves the door open to larger commercial neighbors on the site, so anyone living nearby should watch what gets built.

a894c46e45031baa.headline: Drive-thru lane rules held for another meeting
a894c46e45031baa.summary: The council delayed changes to the city code section governing drive-thru lanes.
a894c46e45031baa.impact: Existing drive-thru rules stay as they are. Restaurant and coffee shop developers waiting on the new standards will have to wait longer; nobody else is touched.

a8d9dd8144a1e646.headline: Traffic calming added to priority list
a8d9dd8144a1e646.summary: The council added traffic calming and other traffic-related actions to the city's list of legislative priorities.
a8d9dd8144a1e646.impact: No speed bumps or new signs come from this on its own. It flags traffic as something the city wants to work on; any real change comes later.

a93f6785760ffee7.headline: Fence and buffer rules rewritten
a93f6785760ffee7.summary: The city rewrote its fencing rules, declaring broken, flammable or spite fences unlawful nuisances, adding a split-rail definition, and barring berms or hedges where a wall is required.
a93f6785760ffee7.impact: A fence that is falling apart, or one put up to needle a neighbor, can now be treated as a nuisance and ordered fixed. Staff will bring back separate changes on commercial buffers and fences where the ground drops away.

a94155d70b271b9e.headline: Consent agenda taken up with changes
a94155d70b271b9e.summary: The council took up its consent agenda with the sewer plant bid moved to the discussion list and one set of minutes to be filled out with more context.
a94155d70b271b9e.impact: No outcome is recorded for this version; a fuller amended motion followed. Batch business either way, and none of it lands on a resident.

a97668bac4a23362.headline: Ranches land rezoned for shops and open space
a97668bac4a23362.summary: The council rezoned more than a dozen parcels in The Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties areas, most to commercial-neighborhood zoning, with some as agriculture, open space or foothill housing.
a97668bac4a23362.impact: If you live near these parcels in The Ranches, expect shops and commercial buildings on most of them rather than houses, with a few kept as farmland or open space.

a993efb75d6417ba.headline: New water rights rules for new development
a993efb75d6417ba.summary: The council changed the city's development code to alter how water rights and early-stage concept plans are handled, with amendments made during the meeting.
a993efb75d6417ba.impact: Landowners and builders bringing new projects forward will have to meet the revised water rights requirements. If you are not proposing a development, nothing changes for you.

aa01de8998e8ddcd.headline: 73 acres shift from business park to housing
aa01de8998e8ddcd.summary: The city changed its long-range land use map for 73.03 acres north of SR-73, south of 8000 North and west of Airport Road, from business park and light industry to foothill homes.
aa01de8998e8ddcd.impact: That 73-acre stretch near SR-73 and Airport Road is now planned for houses instead of offices, warehouses and light industry. If you live nearby, expect a residential neighborhood there rather than a jobs district.

aa4d9e1b4696f758.headline: Rezone the land known as QTS-SCL 2
aa4d9e1b4696f758.summary: The council approved a zoning change for the land known as QTS-SCL 2; the motion does not state the acreage or the new zoning.
aa4d9e1b4696f758.impact: The change resets what can legally be built on that property. The record here does not say where the land is or what the new zoning allows.

aba14ae8632717df.headline: Development deal with Mountainland Supply approved
aba14ae8632717df.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Mountainland Supply; the motion itself does not state the site, the size, or the terms.
aba14ae8632717df.impact: A development agreement locks in what a builder may do on a specific piece of land. The motion doesn't say where that land is or what is going up, so the details sit in the agreement itself.

abbe954fdc6aaba7.headline: Spring Run Plaza decision delayed
abbe954fdc6aaba7.summary: The council set aside the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza instead of voting it up or down.
abbe954fdc6aaba7.impact: If you live near the proposed Spring Run Plaza, nothing is settled: the plan and the zoning change are still open and can come back to the council later.

acf44b8ab1af5acf.headline: Small Business Saturday declared for Nov. 30
acf44b8ab1af5acf.summary: The council proclaimed November 30, 2024 as Small Business Saturday in Eagle Mountain.
acf44b8ab1af5acf.impact: A ceremonial nod to local shops. No rule, fee, or program comes with it.

ad2587863af7fd33.headline: Joshua Biagio joins the Library Advisory Board
ad2587863af7fd33.summary: The council appointed Joshua Biagio to the Library Advisory Board to finish out a term that runs through December 2025.
ad2587863af7fd33.impact: The board advises on library matters and now has a full bench. Nothing changes for you at the library counter.

adc35def3daa6406.headline: Zayo fiber franchise deal put on hold
adc35def3daa6406.summary: The council set aside a franchise agreement that would let Zayo Group run fiber lines through Eagle Mountain right-of-way, with no decision made.
adc35def3daa6406.impact: Nothing changes for you today. The agreement comes back to the council before Zayo gets permission to build in city streets.

ae222e0b73e9e106.headline: Consultant renewal tightened, one item pulled
ae222e0b73e9e106.summary: The council approved the consent agenda after naming David Stewart in a consultant renewal, adding a two meeting a year attendance requirement, and pulling item 15.D for debate.
ae222e0b73e9e106.impact: A batch of routine business cleared in a single vote. The part worth knowing: the Eagle Quest East amendment was lifted out of the batch and argued in the open instead.

ae31f3e2e7e8c582.headline: Youth Council rules rewritten
ae31f3e2e7e8c582.summary: The council rewrote the section of city code that sets up and governs the Youth Council, with revisions worked out earlier the same night.
ae31f3e2e7e8c582.impact: This touches only the teens who serve on the Youth Council and those applying to join. For everyone else it is internal housekeeping.

ae42964763c7aefa.headline: Ground rules set for annexing new land
ae42964763c7aefa.summary: The council adopted an annexation policy plan, the document that sets how Eagle Mountain decides whether to bring neighboring land inside the city.
ae42964763c7aefa.impact: Owners of land just outside the boundary, and anyone hoping to build there, now have a written standard to work from. Inside the current city limits, nothing about your day changes.

ae96096f30375cf4.headline: Downtown Master Plan adopted
ae96096f30375cf4.summary: The council adopted the Downtown Master Plan, the city's guiding document for how its downtown area develops.
ae96096f30375cf4.impact: The plan shapes what gets built downtown in the years ahead, so builders and property owners there will work from it. The motion names no specific project, acreage, or cost.

afe724f7d5fcaf5e.headline: New rules for keeping animals on your property
afe724f7d5fcaf5e.summary: The city set standards for alternative animal management plans and tied the permit to the applicant, so it ends automatically when the property is sold.
afe724f7d5fcaf5e.impact: If you keep animals under one of these plans, the approval is yours, not your land's. It does not transfer to a buyer: when you sell, the new owner has to apply on their own.

afeddd01223f3dc8.headline: Changed water rights developers must hand over
afeddd01223f3dc8.summary: The city changed the rules for the water rights new residential developments must provide before they can build.
afeddd01223f3dc8.impact: This lands on developers bringing new homes to the city, and on how much water the city banks as it grows. The motion doesn't spell out whether the requirement went up or down.

b010fc762d6bd6e5.headline: New sign rules for data center projects
b010fc762d6bd6e5.summary: The city rewrote the part of its sign code covering directional signs for data centers and other large-scale developments, adopting it with edits presented that night.
b010fc762d6bd6e5.impact: The companies behind big projects and the staff reviewing their sign applications work from a different rule now. Homeowners are not asked to do anything.

b02d2399f7d13e06.headline: Shared parking requirement lowered to 35%
b02d2399f7d13e06.summary: The council changed the rules on where parking areas can go and cut the required shared parking from 40% to 35%.
b02d2399f7d13e06.impact: This mainly touches developers and businesses building new commercial projects, which can now share slightly less of their parking. You may see lots laid out differently in future developments.

b04367e7c0e189e0.headline: Crosswalk deal at Woodhaven and Pony Express
b04367e7c0e189e0.summary: The city approved a reimbursement agreement for crosswalk access at Woodhaven Boulevard and Pony Express Parkway and directed staff to address unsafe winter conditions there.
b04367e7c0e189e0.impact: If you cross Pony Express Parkway at Woodhaven on foot, this covers the cost of crosswalk access at that corner, and city staff have been told to deal with what makes it dangerous in winter.

b0521f08c374d170.headline: Hire a firm to run C-PACE loan program
b0521f08c374d170.summary: The council hired Sustainable Real Estate Solutions to handle the paperwork and professional work behind C-PACE projects in Eagle Mountain.
b0521f08c374d170.impact: Commercial property owners who want C-PACE financing for energy or building upgrades now have an administrator to work through. Homeowners are not part of this.

b0785b5369cc6956.headline: Youth Council rules rewritten
b0785b5369cc6956.summary: The council rewrote the Youth Council chapter of city code, moving the power to appoint youth members from the city manager to a committee of advisors.
b0785b5369cc6956.impact: Families with a teen who wants to serve on the Youth Council now apply to that advisory committee. The rest of the city is untouched.

b0a5aad17b6718e2.headline: Discount on a rezone fee turned down
b0a5aad17b6718e2.summary: The council declined Steve McCleery's request to cut the fee for his rezone application from $1,350 to $760.
b0a5aad17b6718e2.impact: Only the applicant is affected. He pays the full $1,350. The city's rezone application fee is unchanged for everyone else.

b16156fdb7ced2b2.headline: Updated transportation impact fee adopted
b16156fdb7ced2b2.summary: An updated transportation impact fee on new development was adopted, along with rules for calculating it, collecting it and appealing it.
b16156fdb7ced2b2.impact: Whoever builds pays this at the permit counter, though the motion does not state the amount. If you are not developing land, nothing on your own bills moves.

b23b3f296f36ccb8.headline: UTA park-and-ride site plan approved
b23b3f296f36ccb8.summary: The council approved the site plan for a UTA park-and-ride lot in Eagle Mountain.
b23b3f296f36ccb8.impact: The transit agency can move ahead with a lot where you would park and catch a bus. The motion gives no location, size, or opening date.

b2fcebc6a52f94cd.headline: Consent agenda approved
b2fcebc6a52f94cd.summary: The council passed its consent agenda as a single batch; the record does not list which items were included.
b2fcebc6a52f94cd.impact: Consent items are the routine business the council approves together without separate debate. The record here doesn't say what was in this batch.

b3611653e5b6e9e0.headline: Changes to the city zoning code adopted
b3611653e5b6e9e0.summary: The council amended Title 17, the city's zoning code, adopting the updated version included in the meeting packet.
b3611653e5b6e9e0.impact: Zoning rules govern what can be built on a property and where. The motion itself doesn't spell out what changed, so the effect on any given property isn't clear from the record.

b72f2754e043b54c.headline: $3,500 a month for a city marketing plan
b72f2754e043b54c.summary: The city hired REDKOR Brand Campaigns to build a marketing and messaging plan at $3,500 a month, capped at 14 months and cancelable at any time.
b72f2754e043b54c.impact: City spending of up to about $49,000 over 14 months, with the economic development work done first. What you would notice is a more consistent look and voice in city communications.

b8114e775c3829bf.headline: Join Utah Valley HOME housing consortium
b8114e775c3829bf.summary: Eagle Mountain signed on to the Utah Valley HOME Consortium, a group of local governments that shares federal housing money.
b8114e775c3829bf.impact: Joining sets up the city to draw on federal housing dollars alongside neighboring cities. Nothing in the motion changes what you pay or what the city offers today.

b92f9957819baafa.headline: Eagle Quest East development change rejected
b92f9957819baafa.summary: The council refused a second amendment to the Eagle Quest East master development agreement, leaving the terms already agreed for that project in force.
b92f9957819baafa.impact: Eagle Quest East proceeds under its existing agreement. What the developer wanted changed is not described in the motion, so the substance of the refusal is not on this record.

ba151c1cad32d50a.headline: Mayor's powers item held until after public comment
ba151c1cad32d50a.summary: The council paused the mayor's powers ordinance until later in the same meeting so that public comment could be reopened first.
ba151c1cad32d50a.impact: Anyone who came to speak about the mayor's duties got the microphone before the council took the item back up. For everyone else, only the order of the agenda moved.

ba8390ec229dbea0.headline: Motion to delay the land decision withdrawn
ba8390ec229dbea0.summary: A move to postpone the same land decision, with direction to work out a better solution with neighboring owners and city staff, was withdrawn.
ba8390ec229dbea0.impact: Nothing was decided here: the motion was taken back before any vote, so it changes nothing for residents.

bb0ce9a5a41a5692.headline: Rewrite of city government rules put on hold
bb0ce9a5a41a5692.summary: The council shelved a rewrite of Title 2, the chapter of city code that sets out how Eagle Mountain governs itself.
bb0ce9a5a41a5692.impact: The current rules on how the city runs stay in force. Nothing on your street or your bill changes, and the record does not say when the rewrite returns.

bbd70251fb86c33b.headline: City land sold at $95,000 an acre
bbd70251fb86c33b.summary: The council cleared the sale of a significant piece of city-owned real property at $95,000 per acre, or $2.18 per square foot.
bbd70251fb86c33b.impact: This settles what the buyer pays, not what goes on the ground. The motion says nothing about future use, so what neighbors will eventually see remains open.

bccbcc538a26dafa.headline: Approve Spring Run Plaza plan and rezone
bccbcc538a26dafa.summary: The council approved the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza, with the land under Roads A and B zoned Agriculture.
bccbcc538a26dafa.impact: This is the approval that lets Spring Run Plaza move forward, so neighbors can expect the project to proceed. The motion doesn't state its size, its uses, or a timeline.

bcf8d65a8fb69c43.headline: Consent agenda approved, website item pulled out
bcf8d65a8fb69c43.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after moving the WDG website change order off it for separate discussion.
bcf8d65a8fb69c43.impact: A batch of pre-cleared items cleared in one vote, with one held back for debate. This is meeting mechanics only.

beefc035773e3fc5.headline: Longer construction hours OK'd for QTS data center
beefc035773e3fc5.summary: The city let the QTS SLC1 data center site run construction outside the hours normally allowed under city code.
beefc035773e3fc5.impact: If you live near the QTS SLC1 site, construction noise may continue outside the usual permitted hours. The motion does not say which hours were granted or how long the exception lasts.

bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.headline: City to sell land at $2.07 a square foot
bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.summary: The council approved selling part of a city-owned parcel at $2.07 per square foot, with the total set by the final survey.
bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.impact: This is a one-off sale of city land and changes nothing at your home. Existing utility easements on the property stay in place, so the lines running through it are protected.

c0a3d421506c569d.headline: Transportation Master Plan put on hold
c0a3d421506c569d.summary: The council delayed adopting the Transportation Master Plan, the city's long-range plan for its road network.
c0a3d421506c569d.impact: No road decisions are locked in by this. The plan shapes where future roads and improvements go, and it has to come back to the council before it takes effect.

c11d4924ea69b4d3.headline: Add transit grants to the state lobbying list
c11d4924ea69b4d3.summary: The council added a study of public transit innovation grants to the city's Legislative Priorities List for the state legislature.
c11d4924ea69b4d3.impact: Nothing changes on the ground. It tells Eagle Mountain's lobbyists what to raise at the Capitol, and any transit money would be years and several votes away.

c1396eb7dc0a7c09.headline: Susan Allen joins Senior Advisory Board
c1396eb7dc0a7c09.summary: The council appointed Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board for a term ending December 31, 2025.
c1396eb7dc0a7c09.impact: Residents who use the city's senior programs gain one more voice advising on them. Otherwise this is a seat being filled.

c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.headline: Consent items approved with changes
c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after narrowing how sponsorship money may be spent, updating the city fee schedule, and setting a Youth City Council quorum.
c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.impact: Mostly housekeeping. The one piece that could reach you is the updated fee schedule, but the motion doesn't say which fees changed or by how much.

c2ef848260675e4a.headline: Youth Council code adopted with mayor voting
c2ef848260675e4a.summary: With the mayor included this time, the council adopted the Youth Council code rewrite handing member appointments to the Youth Council Committee of Advisors.
c2ef848260675e4a.impact: The change now stands as city law. It reaches the teens who join the Youth Council and the staff who run it.

c44f7d719918d940.headline: Jessi Call added as Youth Council advisor
c44f7d719918d940.summary: The council also seated Jessi Call as a Youth City Council advisor, on a term ending May 31, 2027.
c44f7d719918d940.impact: A second volunteer post filled the same evening. Unless a teenager in your house sits on the Youth City Council, you will never run into it.

c470bac794255243.headline: City to push for temporary business sign rules
c470bac794255243.summary: The council added temporary business signage to the city's legislative priorities and asked staff to bring back a proposal.
c470bac794255243.impact: Nothing changes for sign rules yet. Business owners who put out banners or sandwich boards should watch for the staff proposal that follows.

c4c04b5288e2025b.headline: September named PTA Membership Month
c4c04b5288e2025b.summary: The mayor read and the council adopted a proclamation naming September 2024 as Parent Teacher Association Membership Month.
c4c04b5288e2025b.impact: A ceremonial nod to school parent groups. It carries no money, no rules, and no obligation for anyone.

c57d654a03ad9281.headline: Consent list reshuffled before the vote
c57d654a03ad9281.summary: Council members pulled the sewer plant bid off the consent list for its own discussion and ordered two sets of minutes reworded, including the Youth City Council's term.
c57d654a03ad9281.impact: Meeting housekeeping. The one part worth knowing is that the sewer contract got a hearing of its own instead of passing in a batch.

c5a5d089d8c23823.headline: Josh Biagio joins Library Advisory Board
c5a5d089d8c23823.summary: The council appointed Josh Biagio to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.
c5a5d089d8c23823.impact: The last of three library board seats filled for the coming term. There is nothing here for a resident to do or pay.

c6f877e1c66027af.headline: Official city zoning map adopted
c6f877e1c66027af.summary: The council adopted an official zoning map for Eagle Mountain, letting staff fix colors, labels, links to development plans and code, and minor boundary or zone-name errors.
c6f877e1c66027af.impact: The map becomes the single reference for which zone your lot sits in, but adopting it does not change anyone's zoning. Staff can correct a mislabeled boundary without another council vote.

c7473d91a4f0fefa.headline: Eagle Square commercial development approved
c7473d91a4f0fefa.summary: The council approved the preliminary layout for the Eagle Square commercial development, requiring the traffic study be used to place its entrance off Pony Express Parkway.
c7473d91a4f0fefa.impact: A commercial development moves ahead on Pony Express Parkway. Its south entrance must be sited using the traffic study so it lines up with the intersection to the south.

c832a74e1f6d3f2d.headline: Two items pulled for separate discussion
c832a74e1f6d3f2d.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled the civic campus land purchase and the lobbying contract out for individual discussion.
c832a74e1f6d3f2d.impact: This is procedural housekeeping. It only means two items got their own debate instead of passing in a batch.

c91caf5c91462471.headline: $3.5M cut from next year's city budget
c91caf5c91462471.summary: The council adopted the 2026-27 budget after stripping $1 million for the rodeo grounds and $2.5 million for buying land, covering the rest from reserves.
c91caf5c91462471.impact: Rodeo grounds money and the land purchase are off the table for the year ahead. What remains gets paid out of the city's savings rather than from new revenue.

ca8575974ec16800.headline: March named MS Awareness Month
ca8575974ec16800.summary: The council proclaimed March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
ca8575974ec16800.impact: A ceremonial statement with no money or rules attached. Nothing changes for anyone in the city.

cb37ab239acc9a49.headline: City keeps a piece of land it was asked to sell
cb37ab239acc9a49.summary: The council rejected the sale of part of a city-owned Utah County parcel that had been flagged as significant real property.
cb37ab239acc9a49.impact: The land stays in city hands. Unless you live near that parcel or wanted to buy it, this changes nothing you will notice.

cbbf7bad913e0758.headline: Consent items approved, with school traffic conditions
cbbf7bad913e0758.summary: The council approved its consent agenda and attached staff conditions requiring intersection improvements to the John Hancock Charter School west campus item.
cbbf7bad913e0758.impact: Mostly routine housekeeping. The one piece with teeth is that the charter school's west campus must meet the city's conditions on intersection improvements, which matters to people driving near that site.

cbd16e2de476bfa3.headline: New easement rules added to the land use code
cbd16e2de476bfa3.summary: The city added a new easements chapter to its land use code and updated the code's definitions to match.
cbd16e2de476bfa3.impact: This mainly touches property owners and developers dealing with easements, the strips of land set aside for things like utilities or access. Most residents will see no change day to day.

cc05b380718811e6.headline: Consent items approved, two pulled for debate
cc05b380718811e6.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulled items 11.D and 12.A for separate discussion, and added November 5 and December 16 to the 2025 meeting calendar.
cc05b380718811e6.impact: If you want to weigh in on the two pulled items, they get their own discussion rather than passing in a batch. The added dates give you two more 2025 meetings to attend.

ccca5fa20a6b8eb8.headline: Draft FY2026 budget adopted, hearing set for June 3
ccca5fa20a6b8eb8.summary: The council adopted a tentative budget for the 2025-2026 fiscal year and set a public hearing on the final version for June 3, 2025.
ccca5fa20a6b8eb8.impact: Nothing is locked in yet. If you want a say in how the city spends next year's money, June 3 is the date to show up or write in.

cd7f19a7f28a7115.headline: Screening rules for apartment buildings sent back
cd7f19a7f28a7115.summary: The council held off on a change to screening rules for multi-family buildings, asking staff to rework the heat pump and equipment spacing provisions first.
cd7f19a7f28a7115.impact: Nothing takes effect yet. Apartment builders and their architects are the ones waiting on this; the rules they design to stay as they are until the rewrite comes back.

ce234a07251ede47.headline: Concrete form pricing added to lobbying list
ce234a07251ede47.summary: The council put the pricing of concrete forms on the Legislative Priorities List, the running list of issues the city wants worked on.
ce234a07251ede47.impact: A line item on a priorities list, nothing more. Contractors may care about where it leads; residents will not notice it.

ce8dca0a1cf4a8c5.headline: Mid-year budget changes approved
ce8dca0a1cf4a8c5.summary: The council approved the second set of changes to the city's 2024-2025 budget; the record doesn't say which line items changed.
ce8dca0a1cf4a8c5.impact: The record doesn't spell out what changed, so there's no stated effect on your taxes, fees or services. The details sit in the city's budget amendment documents.

cf3d08f7ba130b39.headline: City to sell a small parcel to adjoining owners
cf3d08f7ba130b39.summary: The city approved selling 0.156 acres of city-owned land to the owners of the neighboring lots, with the sale to be finished by February 19, 2026.
cf3d08f7ba130b39.impact: Only the owners of the adjoining lots are affected. They can buy the parcels together on one application, and within six months their fences must sit on the correct lot line or be removed.

cfb2c650bc0473a5.headline: Consent items passed, with a cap on housing loans
cfb2c650bc0473a5.summary: The council approved its consent agenda and added a condition that the mortgage assistance contract with Ultimate Home Lending returns for review if applications pass 100.
cfb2c650bc0473a5.impact: If you apply for the city's mortgage assistance program, an outside firm handles it. Should more than 100 people apply, the council takes another look before it continues.

cfdb11c54689274c.headline: Land swap with the state in the Overland area
cfdb11c54689274c.summary: The city approved trading properties with the state land agency SITLA in the Overland area, on condition the agreement adds matching language and SITLA guarantees clean title.
cfdb11c54689274c.impact: Which parcels the city owns near Overland shifts. Residents will see no immediate change on the ground; what gets built there depends on later decisions.

d0aa16b3e51f4296.headline: Meeting to end by 11 p.m.
d0aa16b3e51f4296.summary: The council set 11:00 p.m. as the hard stop for the evening's meeting.
d0aa16b3e51f4296.impact: Housekeeping for the people in the room. If you were waiting to speak on a late item, it might have been pushed to another night.

d0aeca50b71295f6.headline: Decision delayed on alternative energy zone rules
d0aeca50b71295f6.summary: The council delayed a decision on creating a new Alternative Energy Overlay Zone in the city code.
d0aeca50b71295f6.impact: No rules changed. The proposal comes back to the council another day, so there is still time to weigh in before anything is decided.

d18362cbb276c664.headline: Sales tax growth sent to redevelopment agency
d18362cbb276c664.summary: Growth in sales tax collected inside the Mid-Valley project area will be gathered by the city and handed to its redevelopment agency under an agreement the council approved.
d18362cbb276c664.impact: Nothing changes at the register; the rate you pay is untouched. What changes is which arm of city government ends up holding that money.

d1dc76a647463d18.headline: Development deal for Harmony Subdivision homes
d1dc76a647463d18.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Meritage Homes setting the terms for the Harmony Subdivision.
