d1dc76a647463d18.impact: This locks in the rules Meritage Homes must build to at Harmony. The motion itself doesn't state how many homes, what they cost, or when building starts, so there is nothing yet for neighbors to plan around.

d287ec4f3b999d0d.headline: Consent agenda approved with corrected minutes
d287ec4f3b999d0d.summary: The council passed its consent agenda in one vote, with spelling fixes to the minutes worked out in the earlier work session.
d287ec4f3b999d0d.impact: Housekeeping items cleared in a single batch, plus typo corrections to the meeting record. There is nothing here for a resident to act on.

d28d136d84e6d999.headline: Liquor license rules amended
d28d136d84e6d999.summary: Council members approved an amendment to section 5.15, the city's liquor license code, without the minutes describing what the change does.
d28d136d84e6d999.impact: Businesses that sell alcohol are the ones who deal with this section. The record is too thin to say what is different for them.

d3248c1d81e909c6.headline: Susan Allen's Senior Advisor term confirmed
d3248c1d81e909c6.summary: A second vote confirmed Susan Allen as Senior Advisor for the January 2026 to December 2028 term.
d3248c1d81e909c6.impact: The same appointment, recorded twice. There is nothing here for a resident to act on.

d34546e2ecdb529b.headline: Half-price offer of $45,000 an acre rejected
d34546e2ecdb529b.summary: The council rejected a lower price for the same parcel, $45,000 per acre or $1.03 per square foot, noting it needs no additional water rights.
d34546e2ecdb529b.impact: Had this one carried, the city would have taken less than half as much per acre for the land. It did not, so the higher figure stands.

d379492c19d866fb.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 rezoned to RC
d379492c19d866fb.summary: The council changed the zoning on the Cedar Corners Phase 5 land from residential to the city's RC zone.
d379492c19d866fb.impact: This is the zoning step behind the Cedar Corners Phase 5 project. If you live nearby, what can be built on that land is now governed by RC zone rules instead of the old residential rules.

d420c4bcf28a2417.headline: Sales tax pledged to back redevelopment bonds
d420c4bcf28a2417.summary: The council took up a resolution pledging part of the city's sales tax revenue to repay bonds the city's redevelopment agency plans to issue in 2026.
d420c4bcf28a2417.impact: No new tax and no bill for you. The city would be promising some of its sales tax income to bondholders, money that would otherwise be free for other city spending.

d4c1e66118361b7f.headline: Sale of 0.156-acre city parcel postponed
d4c1e66118361b7f.summary: The council held off on selling a 0.156-acre piece of city-owned land, leaving the terms of the sale undecided.
d4c1e66118361b7f.impact: The city keeps the parcel for now. Unless you live next to it, this one passes you by.

d5db525af3de6295.headline: Industrial zone rules replaced; farm zone tweaked
d5db525af3de6295.summary: The city replaced its industrial zone rules and adjusted the agriculture and commercial storage zones, requiring special approval for equestrian centers and capping moving vehicles at six.
d5db525af3de6295.impact: If you run or plan an equestrian center, a storage yard, or an industrial business, the rules for what you can build and how many trucks you can keep on site have changed. Most residents will notice nothing.

d61cfe930fa6a402.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item moved for discussion
d61cfe930fa6a402.summary: The council cleared its consent agenda, holding three items back for separate votes, shifting Item 13.A. to the discussion portion of the meeting, and correcting spelling in Item 13.B.
d61cfe930fa6a402.impact: Housekeeping that sets the order of the meeting. Nothing about it reaches a resident.

d637bf8739c91d41.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook land rezoned for homes
d637bf8739c91d41.summary: The city rezoned the Cedar Valley Holbrook property from agriculture to foothill residential, on the condition that wildlife corridor fencing be marked on the west side.
d637bf8739c91d41.impact: Land that could only be farmed can now be built with homes. Neighbors will eventually see houses where open agricultural ground is today, with fencing marking the wildlife corridor along the west edge.

d6fa117bfdadac7e.headline: Board liaison assignments put off
d6fa117bfdadac7e.summary: The council kept its 2024 board liaison assignments in place until the mayor can meet with members to set new ones, and asked the city manager for a list of every board that needs a liaison.
d6fa117bfdadac7e.impact: Which councilmember sits in on which board stays as it was last year. Nothing here changes a city service or a bill.

d79e0336ab37cba8.headline: Staff credit card rules put on hold
d79e0336ab37cba8.summary: The council delayed changes to the rules governing city employee credit cards and sent the item back to a work session for more discussion.
d79e0336ab37cba8.impact: This is internal spending policy for city staff. Nothing here reaches your household.

d79e889cb4d263f6.headline: Study a parks and arts sales tax for the fall ballot
d79e889cb4d263f6.summary: Staff were told to study putting a Recreation, Arts and Parks sales tax question on the 2025 municipal election ballot.
d79e889cb4d263f6.impact: If it reaches the ballot in November, you would decide whether to add a small sales tax for parks and arts. Right now this is only research.

d7e0a3a2f87ca7f2.headline: Verizon cell tower site plan approved
d7e0a3a2f87ca7f2.summary: The city approved the site plan for a Verizon communications tower.
d7e0a3a2f87ca7f2.impact: If you live near the site, a new tower is cleared to go up. The motion doesn't say where in the city it will stand.

d832e11d06d2a6ed.headline: Move to reject Hidden Hollow amenity swap
d832e11d06d2a6ed.summary: The council took up a proposal to reject the Hidden Hollow amenity change outright rather than leave it for a later meeting.
d832e11d06d2a6ed.impact: Nothing is settled for Hidden Hollow either way: the amenity change was neither approved nor finally rejected at this meeting.

d8e4e31bf7ee8eaf.headline: City map redrawn for future shops and parks
d8e4e31bf7ee8eaf.summary: The council redrew its long-range land use map for certain Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties parcels, marking most for community commercial and several for parks and open space.
d8e4e31bf7ee8eaf.impact: This is the planning step that lines the city's official map up with the zoning change on those same parcels. For neighbors, it points to shops, parks and open space instead of more housing.

d929de26b7bec679.headline: Pay schedule updated for the city's statutory officers
d929de26b7bec679.summary: The council amended the city code section setting compensation for statutory officers, the positions state law requires Eagle Mountain to fill.
d929de26b7bec679.impact: The motion does not state the new pay figures. It affects a handful of city officers' salaries and does not change any service or bill you receive.

d9d471ec3aae5e3f.headline: Consent items passed, city manager contract pulled
d9d471ec3aae5e3f.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items but pulled the interim city manager agreement with Stephen Mumford and stretched a lobbying consultant's contract to two years.
d9d471ec3aae5e3f.impact: The interim city manager arrangement is left unresolved for now. The rest is administrative cleanup that touches city hall and not your street.

d9fea19b0652cb03.headline: Mayor and council pay raised, starting January
d9fea19b0652cb03.summary: The city set the mayor's pay at $119,800 plus a $600 monthly car allowance and council pay at $18,100 a year, effective January 1, 2025.
d9fea19b0652cb03.impact: This is taxpayer money going to the city's elected officials. The new amounts take effect January 1, 2025; there is no direct change to your bills or services.

da91557fd8eb9772.headline: City's asks of the state legislature set
da91557fd8eb9772.summary: The council adopted its list of priorities to push at the state legislature, adding a matching grant program to be taken up later.
da91557fd8eb9772.impact: This one shapes what the city asks lawmakers for, nothing more. No resident feels it.

dac95bfa458a71ca.headline: City fee schedule updated
dac95bfa458a71ca.summary: The council approved changes to the city's consolidated fee schedule, the master list of what people pay for permits, licenses and city services.
dac95bfa458a71ca.impact: If you pull a permit or pay for a city service, the price may have changed. The motion itself doesn't say which fees moved or by how much.

dad3a2517f272def.headline: Push state for veteran mortgage help
dad3a2517f272def.summary: The council added veterans, active-duty military and public servants to the mortgage assistance program it will ask state lawmakers to support.
dad3a2517f272def.impact: Nothing changes yet. This sets what the city lobbies the Legislature for, so any actual help with a down payment or mortgage would depend on state action later.

dae2a358cf95aedc.headline: Subdivision final plat rules changed
dae2a358cf95aedc.summary: Council members rewrote the city code section governing final plats, the closing paperwork in getting a subdivision approved.
dae2a358cf95aedc.impact: Builders and surveyors filing subdivision paperwork will notice. The motion does not spell out what the new language says, and nobody outside that process is touched by it.

db9159fdf786a630.headline: Parkway Fields phases and layout redrawn
db9159fdf786a630.summary: The council approved a redrawn Parkway Fields plan that splits the townhome phase in two and adds about four townhomes, offset by fewer lots in a later phase.
db9159fdf786a630.impact: The number of homes on the site does not go up. If you are buying there, phase and plat labels changed, and the developer told the council it will dedicate land along Old Airport Road for a trail and trailhead.

dbb70ee232fb274a.headline: Attempt to reject HOME consortium goes nowhere
dbb70ee232fb274a.summary: A move to turn down the Utah Valley HOME Consortium agreement got no support from other council members, so it was never voted on.
dbb70ee232fb274a.impact: The consortium agreement stands. This was an unsuccessful attempt to stop it, not a separate decision reaching residents.

dcb2b6dd0dbc4c15.headline: New water conservation plan adopted
dcb2b6dd0dbc4c15.summary: The council adopted an updated water conservation and management plan for Eagle Mountain, replacing the city's earlier version.
dcb2b6dd0dbc4c15.impact: The plan sets how the city manages and conserves its water supply. Nothing in the motion changes your rates or watering rules today, but it steers future water decisions citywide.

deb37438d3401890.headline: Draft 2026-27 budget accepted, hearings set
deb37438d3401890.summary: The council accepted the tentative city budget for 2026–2027 and set public hearings for June 16, 2026 and August 18, 2026.
deb37438d3401890.impact: No money is locked in yet. If you want a say in how the city spends next year, those two hearing dates are when to show up.

df5c12ce72c47325.headline: Sewer plant will use membrane treatment
df5c12ce72c47325.summary: The council chose membrane bioreactor technology and a construction manager delivery method for the city's planned sewer treatment plant.
df5c12ce72c47325.impact: This locks in how the new sewer plant will be built and what technology treats the city's waste. The cost lands on sewer ratepayers eventually, though no price was set here.

dfa6b60515fc7bbb.headline: Interim budget and proposed tax rate adopted
dfa6b60515fc7bbb.summary: The council adopted an interim budget for the 2026-2027 fiscal year and the proposed certified tax rate, and dropped the city's DebtBook software service.
dfa6b60515fc7bbb.impact: This keeps the city funded until a final budget is adopted and sets the property tax rate the city is proposing. The motion states no dollar figures.

e0bebb6adf467ca1.headline: Hotel height and parking rules put on hold
e0bebb6adf467ca1.summary: The council delayed changes that would let hotels rise above the city's 50-foot limit and provide fewer parking stalls, waiting until the hotel feasibility study is finished.
e0bebb6adf467ca1.impact: No hotel was approved or blocked here. The current rules stand, so a developer wanting a four-story hotel still runs into the height cap and the stall-per-bed count until the study comes back.

e135c6867636244a.headline: Recruiting consultants' contract put off
e135c6867636244a.summary: The council set aside a professional service agreement with recruitment consultants Jason Walker and David Kitchen rather than voting it up or down.
e135c6867636244a.impact: Hiring help for the city waits for a later meeting. Nothing here reaches a resident.

e176e09fe57af0ea.headline: Public art plan adopted
e176e09fe57af0ea.summary: Eagle Mountain adopted a public art plan, the city's written guide for art in public spaces. No money was attached to the motion.
e176e09fe57af0ea.impact: The plan by itself buys nothing and commissions nothing. City staff and anyone proposing public art now have a document to work from; the rest of the city sees no change.

e1809490a455a781.headline: Consent agenda passed, four items pulled out
e1809490a455a781.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, moved three of them into the discussion portion of the meeting and struck a fourth from the agenda.
e1809490a455a781.impact: Meeting mechanics only. Pulling an item means the council argued it separately rather than passing it in the batch, and one item came off the agenda without being decided.

e18a3fbe3d10b9eb.headline: Fees changed for sewer, storm water, and building
e18a3fbe3d10b9eb.summary: The city amended its fee schedule, changing code enforcement fines, building department fees, sewer rates, and storm water charges.
e18a3fbe3d10b9eb.impact: Sewer and storm water charges are part of your city utility bill, so this reaches every household; the building and enforcement changes hit anyone pulling a permit or cited for a violation. The motion doesn't state the new amounts.

e1dd54be7a8a0438.headline: Parkway Fields development agreement amended
e1dd54be7a8a0438.summary: The council updated the master development agreement behind Parkway Fields, the Ault Farms project, so the contract matches the site's revised plan.
e1dd54be7a8a0438.impact: This is the contract that fixes what the builder owes the city there. Buyers and neighbors in Parkway Fields are the ones it reaches; the rest of the city will not notice.

e39a937831c488c7.headline: City protests Cedar Fort annexation of Red Cedar land
e39a937831c488c7.summary: The council formally objected to Red Cedar Corporation's petition, filed July 27, to annex its land into the neighboring Town of Cedar Fort.
e39a937831c488c7.impact: No street, bill or service changes because of this. The council is staking Eagle Mountain's claim in a boundary fight with a neighboring town, and where that land ends up gets settled later, not by this vote.

e3aae1156fe3f502.headline: Primary election results certified, six advance to November
e3aae1156fe3f502.summary: The council certified the August 12 primary results, putting mayoral candidates Melissa Clark and Jared R. Gray and four council candidates on the November 4 ballot.
e3aae1156fe3f502.impact: Your November ballot is now set: two names for mayor, four for city council. Turnout was 25.5%, with 116 mailed ballots arriving too late to count, so watch the postmark deadline in the fall.

e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.headline: Ask the state to fund a sidewalk near Walmart
e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.summary: The council added construction of a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near Walmart to the list of priorities it takes to state lawmakers.
e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.impact: Nothing is built or funded yet. This only puts the sidewalk on the city's ask list. If the state pays for it, people walking near Walmart get a sidewalk.

e42b3fd490442908.headline: Lot size mixture rule shelved
e42b3fd490442908.summary: The council set aside a proposed code section on mixing lot sizes in residential zones, leaving the current rules in place.
e42b3fd490442908.impact: Builders planning subdivisions were the audience for this rule, and they keep working under today's code until the council picks it back up.

e44be31c3f0bb8af.headline: Third change to this year's budget
e44be31c3f0bb8af.summary: For the third time this budget year, the council changed the city's 2023-2024 spending plan, though the motion lists no dollar amounts.
e44be31c3f0bb8af.impact: What moved, and by how much, is not stated in the record of this vote. You would need the amendment document itself to see which accounts changed.

e461251be4e585cf.headline: Council limits mayor's power to set policy
e461251be4e585cf.summary: The council wrote into code that neither the mayor nor staff may enact city policy without a majority council vote, and that no member may speak for the full body.
e461251be4e585cf.impact: City policy now has to clear a public council vote before it takes effect, so more of it happens in front of you at a meeting. Liaison assignments also go to a council vote rather than the mayor alone.

e48e947a787617a3.headline: Bryan Free added as planning commission alternate
e48e947a787617a3.summary: Bryan Free was appointed an alternate on the planning commission, finishing a two-year term that runs through December 2025.
e48e947a787617a3.impact: Alternates fill in when a regular commissioner cannot attend a zoning or development hearing. Filling the seat changes no rule you live under.

e4e946b31067d6d2.headline: Jared Gray named mayor pro tempore
e4e946b31067d6d2.summary: The council picked Councilmember Jared Gray as mayor pro tempore, the member who steps in when the mayor cannot preside.
e4e946b31067d6d2.impact: Nothing changes for households. The title matters only on the rare night the mayor is away from the dais.

e5fa836dc05db55d.headline: 672-acre development deal near the data centers
e5fa836dc05db55d.summary: The council took up a development agreement covering about 672 acres on two parcels, one near the Meta, Google, and QTS sites and one beside the Firefly area.
e5fa836dc05db55d.impact: This touches landowners and neighbors near the data center campuses and in the southwest near Firefly. The council rewrote the buffering language so it only binds land once that land is annexed into the city.

e6121ee0b6b74fcb.headline: Water rights policy added to lobbying list
e6121ee0b6b74fcb.summary: The council directed staff to work with it on a policy covering paper water rights and prioritization dates, adding the item to the Legislative Priorities List.
e6121ee0b6b74fcb.impact: Nothing changes for households yet. Water rights rules eventually shape who can build and how much water the city can promise, but this step only starts the policy work.

e720a89cb623a7a3.headline: Denser housing allowed at Cedar Corners Phase 5
e720a89cb623a7a3.summary: The council changed the city's long-range land use map for Cedar Corners Phase 5, moving it from the lower-density residential category to the next one up.
e720a89cb623a7a3.impact: If you live near Cedar Corners, expect smaller lots and more homes per acre than the old map allowed when this phase is built. The change is to the plan, so nothing breaks ground yet.

e854f84a97214b26.headline: Updated water conservation plan adopted
e854f84a97214b26.summary: The council adopted an amended water conservation and management plan for the city.
e854f84a97214b26.impact: The plan sets how Eagle Mountain manages and conserves its water supply. The motion itself names no new restriction or charge, so watch for the plan's specifics before assuming your watering habits change.

e8a7409ac69f7fc7.headline: Up to $230M in water and sewer bonds
e8a7409ac69f7fc7.summary: The council authorized borrowing up to $230 million by issuing water and sewer revenue bonds, and set the maximum term, interest rate, and discount for the sale.
e8a7409ac69f7fc7.impact: Revenue bonds are repaid from what the city collects on water and sewer bills rather than from property taxes, so ratepayers ultimately carry this debt. A public hearing is required before the bonds are sold.

e9575ce1c444c10d.headline: New design rules for shops and apartments
e9575ce1c444c10d.summary: The council rewrote the city's design standards for commercial buildings and apartment complexes, updating Chapter 17.72 of the municipal code.
e9575ce1c444c10d.impact: Developers drawing up plans for stores, offices or apartments will have to meet the revised look-and-materials rules. If you are not building one, nothing changes for you.

e9b96549abc6dcf6.headline: Stricter rules for steel fences
e9b96549abc6dcf6.summary: The city set new standards for steel fencing, requiring weathering steel at least 1/8 inch thick, banning corrugated panels, and dropping the annual sealing rule.
e9b96549abc6dcf6.impact: If you put up a steel fence, the city will now check the metal's thickness when you pull your permit, corrugated panels are no longer allowed, and you no longer have to seal it every year.

eb3ae48f03a35267.headline: Dillon Boss joins the Library Advisory Board
eb3ae48f03a35267.summary: Dillon Boss was appointed to the Library Advisory Board for a one-year term through December 2024 and sworn in at the meeting.
eb3ae48f03a35267.impact: An advisory seat is filled. Library users will see the same hours, books and staff as before.

eb888342c0eab8c1.headline: Mary Hammond joins Senior Citizens Advisory Council
eb888342c0eab8c1.summary: The council appointed Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, finishing out a four-year term that runs through 2025.
eb888342c0eab8c1.impact: One volunteer seat advising the city on senior issues gets filled. Nothing about it reaches your household.

ec49bd5e3e123e43.headline: Development agreement with Meta approved
ec49bd5e3e123e43.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Stadion, LLC, the company known as Meta, setting the terms for its Eagle Mountain project.
ec49bd5e3e123e43.impact: This sets the ground rules for what Meta may build here and what it owes the city. The motion doesn't list those terms, so residents won't see anything change day to day.

ec5654790d88548e.headline: New rules for fences and privacy screening
ec5654790d88548e.summary: The city amended its code covering fences, privacy screening, and the table of land uses allowed in each zone; the motion does not state what specifically changed.
ec5654790d88548e.impact: If you are planning a fence or a screening wall on your property, the rules you have to build to have changed, so check the current code before you start.

ed21c804323e671e.headline: Laura Jensen named Planning Commission alternate
ed21c804323e671e.summary: The council appointed Laura Jensen as an alternate on the Planning Commission for a three-year term running from May 2026 to March 2029.
ed21c804323e671e.impact: The Planning Commission reviews zoning and development proposals, so an alternate fills in when a regular member is absent. Filling the seat affects nothing you pay or do.

ed5174ede43e72a8.headline: Franchise deal approved for SummitIG Fiber
ed5174ede43e72a8.summary: The council approved a franchise agreement with SummitIG Fiber, LLC, the arrangement a telecom company needs before it can operate in Eagle Mountain.
ed5174ede43e72a8.impact: Nothing here lands on your street or your bill. The terms sit between the city and the company, and the motion itself spells out none of them.

ed82aab2c197cf10.headline: 2025-26 city budget and tax rate adopted
ed82aab2c197cf10.summary: The council adopted Eagle Mountain's budget for the 2025-26 fiscal year and set the property tax rate at the certified rate.
ed82aab2c197cf10.impact: This is the spending plan for the year ahead and the rate behind your city property tax bill. The certified rate is the state-calculated baseline, so the city did not raise taxes above it.

edb99e343e2d8c8e.headline: Bypass Road land sale put on hold
edb99e343e2d8c8e.summary: The council delayed a decision on selling up to 20.35 acres of city-owned land known as the Bypass Road.
edb99e343e2d8c8e.impact: The city keeps the 20.35 acres for now. Any sale would have to come back to the council before it could go through.

eeae61b2ad0e4c58.headline: Consent agenda approved in one vote
eeae61b2ad0e4c58.summary: The council passed its consent agenda, the bundle of items handled together without separate discussion.
eeae61b2ad0e4c58.impact: The record here does not list what was in the bundle, so there is nothing a resident can act on.

efbacf0276cd6a16.headline: Parks and trails master plan sent back for changes
efbacf0276cd6a16.summary: The council delayed adopting the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan and sent it back to the consultant for revisions before a future work session.
efbacf0276cd6a16.impact: No park or trail is affected yet. The plan meant to guide future park and trail decisions is still being reworked and returns to the council later.

f000adff3dc5edb3.headline: Inland port proposal put on hold
f000adff3dc5edb3.summary: The council set aside a resolution backing a Utah Inland Port Authority project area in Eagle Mountain, holding it for more discussion.
f000adff3dc5edb3.impact: Nothing is settled about an inland port here. If the idea concerns or interests you, the debate is still open and will come back to the council.

f07957dd68d40239.headline: Alternative energy overlay zone created
f07957dd68d40239.summary: The council added an alternative energy overlay zone to the city code and put appeals of staff decisions before elected members rather than an administrator.
f07957dd68d40239.impact: Energy developers gain a zoning route to apply through that did not exist before, and contested decisions go to the council. No specific project was approved by this vote.

f10518dcbb90547f.headline: Brent Strong seated on the Planning Commission
f10518dcbb90547f.summary: The council agreed to Brent Strong serving a three-year Planning Commission term, January 2026 through December 2028.
f10518dcbb90547f.impact: Another seat filled on the board that hears zoning and subdivision requests first. Day to day, this changes nothing for you.

f2143c224ba5b9b3.headline: Mid-year changes to the city budget
f2143c224ba5b9b3.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the 2025-2026 city budget, the mid-year rewrite of what the city plans to spend.
f2143c224ba5b9b3.impact: Budget amendments move or add money partway through the year. This motion does not say which line items changed, so the detail lives in the budget document rather than the vote itself.

f2181e8f715eb4f8.headline: RVs and trailers barred from front yards
f2181e8f715eb4f8.summary: The council barred RVs, trailers, farm vehicles and other vehicles from front yards, except on a paved or gravel driveway or the garage side setback.
f2181e8f715eb4f8.impact: If you keep a camper or a trailer parked on the grass out front, that is now off limits. The driveway and the strip beside the garage remain open to you. Every residential zone is covered.

f22cc91c54e549db.headline: Consent agenda approved
f22cc91c54e549db.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote; the record here does not list which items were on it.
f22cc91c54e549db.impact: Consent items are the ones the council has already agreed are uncontroversial enough to pass together. Without a list of what was included, there is nothing here a resident can act on.

f31f4cd41d8c1c77.headline: Consent agenda passed, one item pulled
f31f4cd41d8c1c77.summary: The council cleared its batch of routine items in one vote, holding item 12.C for a later meeting and attaching an annual review to item 12.E.
f31f4cd41d8c1c77.impact: The held item returns to a future agenda. For residents this is bookkeeping, though item 12.E will now come back for a look once a year.

f46007953488584e.headline: Lacie Messerly named city recorder
f46007953488584e.summary: Lacie Messerly was appointed as Eagle Mountain City Recorder.
f46007953488584e.impact: The recorder keeps the city's official records and meeting minutes. If you request a public document, this is the office you deal with.

f51421a986885893.headline: Residential zoning rewrite rejected
f51421a986885893.summary: The council turned down proposed changes to the city's definitions and residential zone rules.
f51421a986885893.impact: Rules for residential lots stay as they are. Anyone who was counting on the proposed change, builders in particular, goes back to the existing code.

f536bfdaf55667cd.headline: Zoning changed on a list of properties
f536bfdaf55667cd.summary: The council approved general plan and zoning changes for the properties listed on a chart, with each parcel rezoned according to the proposed rezoning map.
f536bfdaf55667cd.impact: Owners of the listed parcels, and their neighbors, are the people this reaches: what can be built there changes. The record names a chart rather than addresses, so check the meeting packet for your parcel.

f63342b5e7e2ce67.headline: Historic zones rules put off to August
f63342b5e7e2ce67.summary: The council delayed a new set of rules for historic zones a second time, sending it to the August 6 meeting.
f63342b5e7e2ce67.impact: Owners of older properties waiting to learn which rules apply to them wait another month. Everyone else can skip this one.

f6a4a26cf9804ad4.headline: Tentative 2024-25 budget adopted, hearing June 4
f6a4a26cf9804ad4.summary: The council tentatively adopted the city's 2024-2025 budget and set a June 4, 2024 public hearing before the final budget is adopted.
f6a4a26cf9804ad4.impact: The June 4 hearing is your chance to speak on next year's city spending before the council locks it in.

f7618e5e6217129c.headline: Eagle Crest Storage facility approved
f7618e5e6217129c.summary: The city signed off on the site plan for Eagle Crest Storage, clearing the way for the storage facility to be built.
f7618e5e6217129c.impact: People living near the site will see a storage facility go up. The motion doesn't say exactly where it sits or how large it is.

f79112668047830b.headline: New rules for political and temporary signs
f79112668047830b.summary: The council rewrote the sign rules covering political and temporary signs, dropped the proposed seasonal sign language, and told staff to draft temporary sign terms for business licenses.
f79112668047830b.impact: Both the sign you stake in your yard at election time and the banner outside a shop fall under this. Business owners face one more temporary sign requirement once staff bring the licensing language back.

f8c69fd69739e785.headline: Consent agenda approved in one vote
f8c69fd69739e785.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items handled together without separate discussion.
f8c69fd69739e785.impact: Consent items are the ones the council considers uncontroversial enough to pass in a single vote. The motion text does not list what was included.

f922ac59e1387b98.headline: Noise and nuisance rules sent back to staff
f922ac59e1387b98.summary: The council held off on changes to the city's nuisance and noise rules, sending them back to staff for revisions and a return at the next meeting.
f922ac59e1387b98.impact: The current noise and nuisance rules stay in force for now. If you have been following this one, the debate picks up again at the next council meeting.

f92496c7fbe3b1c2.headline: Facilities master plan left unsettled
f92496c7fbe3b1c2.summary: A proposal to treat the Galloway report as a guide toward a future city facilities master plan drew no support, and the council took no action on it.
f92496c7fbe3b1c2.impact: How the city plans its buildings for the years ahead stays undecided. Nothing shifts for residents unless the council picks the question back up.

f9e4bc6085db8fdb.headline: Rod Hess appointed to Planning Commission
f9e4bc6085db8fdb.summary: The council seated Rod Hess on the Planning Commission for a three-year term through December 2026.
f9e4bc6085db8fdb.impact: That seat reviews zoning changes and subdivision plans before they reach the council, so anyone building or living beside new development eventually meets its recommendations.

fa21fe9624eac176.headline: Affordable housing plan put off
fa21fe9624eac176.summary: The council delayed adopting the city's affordable housing plan, asking for the changes it discussed before voting.
fa21fe9624eac176.impact: The city's plan for lower-cost housing is not settled yet. Anyone watching housing costs here will have to wait for a future meeting.

faaef005a15d917b.headline: Noise limits now lift at 7 a.m. instead of 9 a.m.
faaef005a15d917b.summary: The city changed its noise rules, adjusting maximum decibel levels during restricted hours and moving the morning cutoff from 9 a.m. to 7 a.m., seven days a week.
faaef005a15d917b.impact: This applies citywide, weekends included: the stricter noise limits now end at 7 a.m. rather than 9 a.m., so you may hear louder activity two hours earlier in the morning.

faf564d49fb2618d.headline: Three items pulled off the consent list
faf564d49fb2618d.summary: The council approved its batch of consent items but pulled three of them out for discussion later in the meeting.
faf564d49fb2618d.impact: This is a scheduling move: those three items get talked through in the open rather than passing in a bundle. Nothing about the decisions themselves changed here.

fb214cd216ff5000.headline: Animal shelter alternatives added to lobbying list
fb214cd216ff5000.summary: The council added work with Best Friends Animal Society, and the resources that group presented, to the city's list of legislative priorities.
fb214cd216ff5000.impact: This shapes what the city asks state lawmakers for. Nothing changes at the animal shelter or on your street because of this vote.

fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.headline: Jessie Southworth appointed to Community Services
fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.summary: The council appointed Jessie Southworth to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, April 2026 through March 2029.
fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.impact: A volunteer seat gets an occupant. There is no change to any city service attached to it.

fbc813f79adcfb5f.headline: Firefly water tank change order put off
fbc813f79adcfb5f.summary: The council set aside a second change order on the Firefly 4 million gallon water tank without deciding it.
fbc813f79adcfb5f.impact: The tank work waits on a later meeting for this piece. Nothing about your water service changes in the meantime.

fe9f6b250ca5fcce.headline: Enyo battery site rezoned to agriculture
fe9f6b250ca5fcce.summary: The council changed the zoning on the Enyo battery property from airpark to agriculture.
fe9f6b250ca5fcce.impact: Airpark uses are off the table on that ground now. Neighbors of the site are the ones who would see a difference; the rest of the city will not.

ff157f1cb6f92b8b.headline: Eagle Square commercial plans put off
ff157f1cb6f92b8b.summary: The council delayed a decision on the preliminary plat for the Eagle Square commercial project.
ff157f1cb6f92b8b.impact: Neither approved nor refused, the project sits where it is until the council takes the item back up. Nothing changes at the site in the meantime.

ffb8d6cc826597a7.headline: City budget amended for 2024-25
ffb8d6cc826597a7.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's 2024-2025 annual budget; the motion does not say which line items changed.
ffb8d6cc826597a7.impact: Budget amendments redirect real money mid-year. The motion itself names no amounts or projects, so the budget document is where to look for what actually shifted.
